docs.title: iranquant
docs.text:
Async-first TSETMC + Codal market-data client for the Iranian capital market.

iranquant uses the same JSON endpoints as the TSETMC web terminal and reconstructs Codal's embedded var datasource tables into DataFrames. It provides a synchronous API for scripts and an async API for production services, with Pandas or Polars output, a quant analytics engine and a market watcher.

import iranquant as iq

frame = iq.history("فولاد", adjust="all")
print(frame.tail())

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text: Area Description Async and sync One pooled httpx transport with retries, a concurrency semaphore and TLS fallbacks. The sync wrapper works inside Jupyter/Colab event loops. Codal parsing Tables are read from the raw var datasource = {...} JSON with a brace-balanced parser; no HTML selectors are involved. Pydantic V2 Wire payloads are validated by models that tolerate fields added by TSETMC. Pandas and Polars Every public function accepts engine="pandas" (default) or engine="polars" and returns that engine type. Price adjustment Backward gap-ratio adjustment (adjust="all") and ex-rights capital-increase adjustment (adjust="capital_only"). Quant analytics Buyer power, per-capita values, smart-money entry/exit, multi-timeframe Kaufman efficiency, ZigZag swing legs and a vectorized screener. Monthly sales Extracts current-month, YTD and prior-year sales from the standard تولید و فروش table and computes MoM/YoY growth. CLI iranquant search, history, screener, indices and codal --parse-latest, rendered with Rich tables. Watcher MarketWatch polling with BUY_QUEUE_LOCKED, BUY_QUEUE_BROKEN, SELL_QUEUE_LOCKED, SELL_QUEUE_BROKEN and VOLUME_SPIKE events. Networking Environment proxies are ignored by default; *.codal.ir uses a certificate-relaxed transport and TSETMC gets an HTTP/1.1 no-verify fallback.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install iranquant

From a checkout:

python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ".[dev,docs]"

Requirements: Python 3.10+, httpx, pydantic>=2.7, tenacity, jdatetime, pandas, polars and pyarrow.

docs.title: Quick example
docs.text:
import iranquant as iq

code = iq.get_inscode("فولاد")                       # "46348559193224090"
daily = iq.history(code, adjust="all")              # 11 clean OHLCV columns
full = iq.full_history("فولاد")                     # + real/legal client data
market = iq.market_watch()                          # one request, whole market
flow = iq.money_flow("فولاد")                       # smart-money columns

Use Polars anywhere with engine="polars":

daily = iq.history("فولاد", engine="polars")
print(type(daily))  # <class 'polars.dataframe.frame.DataFrame'>

docs.text:
• Quickstart — a five-minute sync and async tutorial, including proxy and split-tunneling tips for Iran.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: Get from zero to adjusted candles, Codal tables and live events in about five minutes.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
pip install iranquant

For a development checkout with the docs toolchain:

python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ".[dev,docs]"

docs.title: 2. Resolve a symbol and fetch history
docs.text:
SynchronousAsynchronous 
import iranquant as iq

code = iq.get_inscode("فولاد")
print(code)  # "46348559193224090"

frame = iq.history(code, adjust="all")
print(frame.columns.tolist())
# ['date', 'jdate', 'open', 'high', 'low', 'close',
#  'final_price', 'prev_price', 'volume', 'value', 'trades']

print(frame.tail(3)[["jdate", "close", "final_price", "volume"]])

import asyncio
import iranquant as iq

async def main() -> None:
    async with iq.AsyncIranQuant(timeout=20.0, max_concurrency=8) as client:
        code = await client.resolve("فولاد")
        frame = await client.history(code, adjust="all")
        print(frame.tail(3)[["jdate", "close"]])

asyncio.run(main())

The async client owns one pooled transport; reuse it for many symbols instead of creating a new client per call.

docs.title: 3. Switch to Polars
docs.text:
Every function accepts engine="polars" and returns a polars.DataFrame:

import iranquant as iq

frame = iq.full_history("فولاد", engine="polars")
print(frame.select(["jdate", "close", "buy_I_Volume"]).tail(3))

docs.title: 4. Join retail and institutional flows
docs.text:
full = iq.full_history("فولاد")
print(full[["jdate", "buy_I_Volume", "sell_I_Volume",
            "buy_N_Volume", "sell_N_Volume"]].tail())

Columns prefixed with I are individual/retail (حقیقی) and N are institutional/legal (حقوقی).

docs.title: 7. Screen the live market
docs.text:

market = iq.market_watch()                 # one request for the whole market
screener = iq.MarketScreener(market)

buy_locked = screener.filter_buy_queue()

docs.title: 8. Watch transitions in real time
docs.text:
import asyncio
from iranquant import MarketWatcher
from iranquant.stream import BUY_QUEUE_LOCKED, VOLUME_SPIKE

async def main() -> None:
    watcher = MarketWatcher()

    @watcher.on_event(BUY_QUEUE_LOCKED)
    def on_lock(event):
        print("buy queue locked:", event.symbol, event.data["buy_queue_volume"])

    @watcher.on_event(VOLUME_SPIKE)
    async def on_spike(event):
        print("volume spike:", event.symbol, event.data["delta"])

    async for event in watcher.watch(
        interval=3.0,
        symbols=["فولاد", "خودرو"],
        only_market_hours=True,          # Sat-Wed, 09:00-12:30 Tehran
    ):
        print(event.event_type, event.symbol)

asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: 9. Cache incrementally
docs.text:
from iranquant import history
from iranquant.core.cache import ParquetCache

cache = ParquetCache()                   # ~/.cache/iranquant
combined = cache.update("fold-history", history("فولاد"))
print(combined.tail())

See Caching & Polars for the full workflow.

docs.title: 10. Use the command line
docs.text:
Installing the package registers an iranquant command backed by Rich tables and colour coding:

iranquant search فولاد
iranquant history فولاد --days 15 --adjust all
iranquant screener --mode buy-queue --limit 20
iranquant screener --mode tick-surge
iranquant indices
iranquant codal فولاد
iranquant codal فولاد --parse-latest

codal --parse-latest prints the report's tables and a monthly sales summary in million Rials, including MoM and YoY growth.

docs.title: Proxy, VPN and split-tunneling in Iran
docs.text:
Iranian market hosts (cdn.tsetmc.com, tsetmc.com, codal.ir, search.codal.ir) are domestic and are usually fastest and most reliable when they bypass your VPN. iranquant is built around that reality.

Environment proxies are ignored by default

AsyncHTTPClient uses trust_env=False unless you pass proxy=.... This prevents HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY exported by VPN or corporate clients from silently routing domestic .ir traffic through a remote HTTP port.

docs.title: Option A — explicit proxy (only when you need it)
docs.text:
import iranquant as iq

async with iq.AsyncIranQuant(proxy="http://127.0.0.1:9090") as client:
    df = await client.history("فولاد")

docs.title: Option B — split tunneling (recommended for servers)
docs.text:
Configure your VPN client so that domestic destinations bypass the tunnel. For example, with WireGuard AllowedIPs = 0.0.0.0/0, ::/0 you can exclude routes with ip route add <domestic CIDR> via <local-gateway>, or use your VPN app's "split tunneling / bypass LAN and domestic sites" toggle. Add at minimum:

  • cdn.tsetmc.com
  • tsetmc.com
  • codal.ir and *.codal.ir
  • your DNS resolver, if it is queried over the tunnel

docs.title: Option C — run on an Iranian server
docs.text:
If your production host sits inside Iran, leave proxy=None and let the library connect directly. On SSL/proxy-style failures:

  • *.tsetmc.com is retried once over an HTTP/1.1, certificate-relaxed transport;
  • *.codal.ir always uses its dedicated certificate-relaxed transport because its chain frequently fails strict verification.

Market hours

TSETMC sessions run Saturday–Wednesday, 09:00–12:30 Tehran time. Use only_market_hours=True in MarketWatcher.watch() to avoid pointless polling outside those hours.

docs.title: راهنمای فارسی iranquant
docs.text: iranquant یک کتابخانهٔ ناهمگام (async) برای دریافت دادهٔ بازار سرمایهٔ ایران از TSETMC و کدال است. یک API همگام (sync) ساده نیز دارد که در اسکریپت‌ها و محیط‌های Jupyter/Colab بدون خطای event loop کار می‌کند. خروجی می‌تواند Pandas یا Polars باشد.

docs.title: نصب
docs.text:
pip install iranquant

برای نصب از مخزن و همراه با ابزار توسعه و مستندات:

python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ".[dev,docs]"

نیازمندی‌ها: پایتون ۳٫۱۰ یا بالاتر، httpx، pydantic>=2.7، tenacity، jdatetime، pandas، polars و pyarrow.

docs.title: جست‌وجوی نماد و کد نماد (insCode)
docs.text:
import iranquant as iq

results = iq.search("فولاد")
full_name = results.iloc[0]["company_name"]

code = iq.get_inscode("فولاد")   # "46348559193224090"

نکته‌ها:

  • حروف عربی (ي، ك، ة) و ارقام فارسی به‌صورت خودکار یکسان‌سازی می‌شوند.
  • اگر ورودی عددی باشد (مثل 46348559193224090)، بدون تماس شبکه‌ای برگردانده می‌شود.
  • نمادهای دارای flow فعال (۱، ۲ یا ۴) در اولویت هستند و در صورت تساوی، جدیدترین lastDate انتخاب می‌شود.
  • نتیجه‌ها در حافظهٔ همان فرایند cache می‌شوند. برای پاک‌سازی:
from iranquant.market.symbol import clear_cache
clear_cache()

docs.title: تاریخچهٔ روزانه و تعدیل قیمت
docs.text:
daily = iq.history("فولاد", adjust="all")
full = iq.full_history("فولاد")            # + دادهٔ حقیقی/حقوقی
clients = iq.client_type("فولاد")          # فقط حقیقی/حقوقی

ستون‌های history:

ستون نوع معنی date datetime.date تاریخ میلادی jdate str تاریخ شمسی YYYY-MM-DD open float قیمت باز شدن high float بیشترین قیمت low float کمترین قیمت close float آخرین قیمت معامله final_price float قیمت پایانی prev_price float قیمت پایانی روز قبل (تعدیل‌نشده) volume float حجم معاملات value float ارزش معاملات (ریال) trades float تعداد معاملات

حالت‌های تعدیل:

مقدار adjust رفتار "none" قیمت‌های خام TSETMC "all" تعدیل کامل عقب‌رو برای سود نقدی و افزایش سرمایه "capital_only" تعدیل عقب‌رو فقط برای افزایش سرمایه

فرمول تعدیل کامل (all): برای هر روز i نسبت r[i] = prev_price[i+1] / final_price[i] و ضریب تجمعی F[i] = F[i+1] * r[i] محاسبه می‌شود (روز آخر ضریب ۱ دارد) و همهٔ ستون‌های قیمتی در آن ضرب می‌شوند.

فرمول تعدیل افزایش سرمایه (capital_only): برای هر رویداد از numberOfShareOld به numberOfShareNew، ردیف‌های قبل از تاریخ رویداد در نسبت old / new ضرب می‌شوند.

raw = iq.history("فولاد", adjust="none")
adj = iq.history("فولاد", adjust="all")
cap = iq.history("فولاد", adjust="capital_only")

docs.title: پول هوشمند و قدرت حرکت
docs.text:
flow = iq.money_flow("فولاد")            # buy power + smart money
power = iq.movement_power("فولاد")       # امتیاز چندبازه‌ای

print(flow[["jdate", "buyer_power_ratio",
            "smart_money_entry", "smart_money_exit"]].tail())
print(power[["jdate", "er_5", "er_20", "er_60",
             "movement_power_score"]].tail())

docs.title: جریان پول (money flow)
docs.text:
ستون‌های محاسبه‌شده:

  • real_buy_per_capita و real_sell_per_capita: سرانهٔ خرید/فروش حقیقی (ریال).
  • real_buy_per_capita_m و real_sell_per_capita_m: همان مقدار به میلیون تومان.
  • buyer_power_ratio: نسبت قدرت خریدار حقیقی به فروشنده حقیقی.
  • net_real_value: جریان خالص پول حقیقی (ریال).
  • ownership_change_pct: درصد تغییر مالکیت حقیقی نسبت به کل حجم.
  • close_vs_final_pct: اختلاف آخرین قیمت با قیمت پایانی.
  • vol_ratio: نسبت حجم به میانگین متحرک حجم.
  • smart_money_entry و smart_money_exit: سیگنال‌های ورود/خروج پول هوشمند.

سیگنال ورود وقتی فعال می‌شود که هم‌زمان vol_ratio >= 1.8، buyer_power_ratio >= 1.5، net_real_value > 0 و close >= final_price باشد. سیگنال خروج با buyer_power_ratio <= 0.67، net_real_value < 0 و close <= final_price فعال می‌شود.

docs.title: قدرت حرکت (movement power)
docs.text:
برای هر پنجرهٔ w نسبت کارایی علامت‌دار کافمن محاسبه می‌شود:

er_w = sign(close - close.shift(w))
       * abs(close - close.shift(w))
       / rolling_sum(abs(close.diff()), w)

با سه پنجره، وزن‌ها (0.5, 0.3, 0.2) هستند؛ در غیر این صورت وزن‌ها مساوی‌اند. امتیاز نهایی با یک ضریب حجم (بین ۰٫۵ تا ۲) و در صورت وجود، ضریب قدرت خریدار (بین ۰٫۵ تا ۱٫۵) تعدیل می‌شود و در بازهٔ [-100, +100] قرار می‌گیرد.

# نسخهٔ Polars
import polars as pl
power = iq.movement_power("فولاد", engine="polars")
strong = power.filter(pl.col("movement_power_score") > 50)
print(strong.select(["jdate", "movement_power_score"]).tail())

docs.title: فیلتر لحظه‌ای بازار (Screener)
docs.text:
market = iq.market_watch()
screener = iq.MarketScreener(market)

buy_locked = screener.filter_buy_queue()
sell_locked = screener.filter_sell_queue()
surges = screener.filter_positive_tick_surge(min_diff_pct=1.5)

high_volume = screener.scan_market(
    lambda df: df["volume"] > df["volume"].median()
)

شرط‌ها:

  • filter_buy_queue(): صف خرید، یعنی close >= tmax و حجم صف خرید (zmd) بزرگ‌تر از صفر.
  • filter_sell_queue(): صف فروش، یعنی close <= tmin و حجم صف فروش (zmo) بزرگ‌تر از صفر.
  • filter_positive_tick_surge(min_diff_pct=1.5): آخرین قیمت حداقل ۱٫۵ درصد بالاتر از قیمت پایانی باشد.
  • scan_market(predicate): هر شرط سفارشی روی DataFrame پانداس.

نوع خروجی (Pandas یا Polars) با نوع ورودی یکسان است.

docs.title: استخراج جدول‌های کدال
docs.text:
reports = iq.monthly_reports("فولاد")      # LetterType=58
letter = reports.Letters[0]
tables = iq.codal_report(letter)           # URLها خودکار مطلق می‌شوند

for name, table in tables.items():
    print(name, table.shape)               # «شیت - جدول»
  • LetterType=58 گزارش فعالیت ماهانه و LetterType=6 صورت‌های مالی میان‌دوره‌ای است.
  • داده‌ها از شیء var datasource = {...} صفحهٔ گزارش استخراج می‌شوند؛ بدون BeautifulSoup و بدون وابستگی به selectorهای HTML.
  • سلول‌های نامرئی حذف می‌شوند، سطرهای سرستون تشخیص داده می‌شوند، ارقام فارسی به ASCII تبدیل می‌شوند، جداکنندهٔ هزارگان حذف می‌شود، ٫ به نقطه تبدیل می‌شود و پرانتز حسابداری (1,200) به -1200.0 تبدیل می‌شود.
  • ستون‌های تکراری پسوند _2، _3 و کلیدهای جدول تکراری پسوند (2) می‌گیرند.

docs.title: تحلیل خودکار فروش ماهانه
docs.text:
iranquant جدول استاندارد «تولید و فروش» را می‌شناسد و فروش ماه جاری، تجمعی سال مالی، سال قبل و درصد رشد ماهانه/سالانه را برمی‌گرداند (به میلیون ریال):

import iranquant as iq

summary = iq.monthly_sales_summary("فولاد")
print(summary["period_end"])            # «1405-07-30»
print(summary["current_month_sales"])
print(summary["ytd_sales"])
print(summary["prev_ytd_sales"])
print(summary["mom_change_pct"])        # از گزارش ماه قبل
print(summary["yoy_change_pct"])
print(summary["summary_df"])            # فقط سطرهای جمع/مجموع

اگر جدول‌ها را از قبل دارید، از تحلیل‌گر خالص استفاده کنید:

tables = iq.parse_codal_report(letter)   # نام دیگر iq.codal_report
summary = iq.analyze_monthly_sales(tables)

تحلیل‌گر هم Pandas و هم Polars را می‌پذیرد و parse_codal_report گزینهٔ engine="polars" را نیز پشتیبانی می‌کند.

print(len(reports), reports.total, reports.page)
for letter in reports:

latest = reports[0]

docs.title: پخش زندهٔ بازار
docs.text:
import asyncio
from iranquant import MarketWatcher
from iranquant.stream import BUY_QUEUE_LOCKED, VOLUME_SPIKE

async def main() -> None:
    watcher = MarketWatcher()

    @watcher.on_event(BUY_QUEUE_LOCKED)
    def on_lock(event):
        print("صف خرید قفل شد:", event.symbol,
              event.data["buy_queue_volume"])

    @watcher.on_event(VOLUME_SPIKE)
    async def on_spike(event):
        print("جهش حجم:", event.symbol, event.data["delta"])

    async for event in watcher.watch(
        interval=3.0,
        symbols=["فولاد", "خودرو"],
        only_market_hours=True,     # شنبه تا چهارشنبه، ۹:۰۰ تا ۱۲:۳۰ تهران
    ):
        print(event.event_type, event.symbol)

asyncio.run(main())

رویدادها:

رویداد شرط BUY_QUEUE_LOCKED close >= tmax و حجم صف خرید مثبت BUY_QUEUE_BROKEN صف خرید قبلی باز شود SELL_QUEUE_LOCKED close <= tmin و حجم صف فروش مثبت SELL_QUEUE_BROKEN صف فروش قبلی باز شود VOLUME_SPIKE افزایش حجم هر پول >= 1.8x میانگین افزایش‌های قبلی

برای بک‌تست بدون شبکه، از watcher.process_snapshot(snapshot) استفاده کنید که همگام و قطعی است.

docs.title: Cache محلی Parquet
docs.text:
import iranquant as iq
from iranquant.core.cache import ParquetCache

cache = ParquetCache()                     # ~/.cache/iranquant
combined = cache.update("fold-history",
                        iq.history("فولاد", adjust="all"))
print(combined.tail())
  • مکان پیش‌فرض: ~/.cache/iranquant/ (قابل تغییر با متغیر محیطی IRANQUANT_CACHE_DIR یا آرگومان directory).
  • update ردیف‌های جدید را ادغام می‌کند، رکورد تکراری هر تاریخ را با جدیدترین جایگزین می‌کند و خروجی را بر اساس تاریخ مرتب می‌کند.
  • توابع بازار به‌صورت خودکار cache نمی‌نویسند؛ ParquetCache یک ابزار مستقل است تا کلیدها و سیاست نگهداری را خودتان کنترل کنید.

docs.title: خط فرمان (CLI)
docs.text:
با نصب بسته، فرمان iranquant ثبت می‌شود و خروجی را با جدول‌های رنگی Rich نمایش می‌دهد:

iranquant search فولاد
iranquant history فولاد --days 15 --adjust all
iranquant screener --mode buy-queue --limit 20
iranquant screener --mode tick-surge
iranquant indices
iranquant codal فولاد
iranquant codal فولاد --parse-latest

گزینهٔ codal --parse-latest جدول‌های گزارش و خلاصهٔ فروش ماهانه (به میلیون ریال، همراه با رشد ماهانه و سالانه) را چاپ می‌کند.

docs.title: شبکه، VPN و Split-Tunneling در ایران
docs.text:
دامنه‌های داخلی (cdn.tsetmc.com، tsetmc.com، codal.ir و search.codal.ir) معمولاً وقتی از VPN عبور نکنند سریع‌تر و پایدارتر هستند. iranquant بر همین اساس طراحی شده است.

متغیرهای پروکسی محیطی به‌صورت پیش‌فرض نادیده گرفته می‌شوند

AsyncHTTPClient به‌طور پیش‌فرض از trust_env=False استفاده می‌کند تا HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY که VPN یا ابزارهای شرکتی تنظیم کرده‌اند، ترافیک دامنه‌های داخلی را از یک پورت HTTP راه دور عبور ندهد.

docs.title: گزینهٔ ۱: پروکسی صریح (فقط در صورت نیاز)
docs.text:
import iranquant as iq

async with iq.AsyncIranQuant(proxy="http://127.0.0.1:9090") as client:
    df = await client.history("فولاد")

docs.title: گزینهٔ ۲: Split-Tunneling (پیشنهادی برای سرورها)
docs.text:
در کلاینت VPN خود ترافیک مقاصد داخلی را از تونل خارج کنید. برای نمونه در WireGuard با AllowedIPs = 0.0.0.0/0, ::/0 می‌توانید مسیرهای داخلی را با ip route add <domestic CIDR> via <local-gateway> مستثنی کنید، یا در اپ VPN گزینهٔ «split tunneling / bypass LAN and domestic sites» را فعال کنید. حداقل این مقاصد را مستثنی کنید:

  • cdn.tsetmc.com
  • tsetmc.com
  • codal.ir و *.codal.ir
  • سرور DNS شما، اگر از طریق تونل کوئری می‌شود

docs.title: گزینهٔ ۳: اجرا روی سرور داخل ایران
docs.text:
اگر سرور شما داخل ایران است، proxy=None را نگه دارید و اتصال مستقیم برقرار کنید. در صورت خطای SSL یا پروکسی:

  • برای *.tsetmc.com یک بار تلاش دوباره روی ترانسپورت HTTP/1.1 بدون بررسی گواهی انجام می‌شود؛
  • برای *.codal.ir همیشه از ترانسپورت مخصوص با بررسی گواهی آسان‌گیر استفاده می‌شود.

ساعت بازار

جلسات TSETMC شنبه تا چهارشنبه، ۹:۰۰ تا ۱۲:۳۰ به وقت تهران است. برای جلوگیری از درخواست‌های بی‌مورد خارج از این بازه، از only_market_hours=True استفاده کنید.

docs.text:

try:

except iq.SymbolNotFoundError:

except iq.NetworkError:

docs.title: Pandas or Polars, same API
docs.text:
Every public data function accepts engine="pandas" (default) or engine="polars" and returns that engine type:

import iranquant as iq

pandas_frame = iq.history("فولاد")                     # pandas.DataFrame
polars_frame = iq.history("فولاد", engine="polars")    # polars.DataFrame

The quant functions preserve the input engine:

import polars as pl

flow = iq.money_flow("فولاد", engine="polars")
assert isinstance(flow, pl.DataFrame)

entries = flow.filter(pl.col("smart_money_entry"))

This also applies to Codal parsing:

tables = iq.codal_report(letter, engine="polars")

docs.title: Local Parquet cache
docs.text:
ParquetCache stores one Parquet file per logical key under ~/.cache/iranquant/ by default. Override the location with the IRANQUANT_CACHE_DIR environment variable or by passing a directory.

from iranquant.core.cache import ParquetCache

cache = ParquetCache()                     # ~/.cache/iranquant
print(cache.directory)

docs.title: Save and load
docs.text:
import iranquant as iq

frame = iq.history("فولاد")
path = cache.save("fold-history", frame)
print(path)                                # .../fold-history.parquet

loaded = cache.load("fold-history")        # pandas
loaded_pl = cache.load("fold-history", engine="polars")

Unsafe characters in a key are replaced with underscores:

cache.path_for("فولاد/history")
# PosixPath('~/.cache/iranquant/_history.parquet')

docs.title: Incremental updates
docs.text:
update() merges new rows into the cached dataset, keeping the newest row per date and sorting the result. This is the recommended daily workflow:

import iranquant as iq
from iranquant.core.cache import ParquetCache

cache = ParquetCache()

# First run: fetch and persist everything.
full = cache.update("fold-history", iq.history("فولاد", adjust="all"))

# Later runs: fetch again (TSETMC returns the full series) and merge.
# `update` replaces duplicate dates and keeps the series sorted.
combined = cache.update("fold-history", iq.history("فولاد", adjust="all"))
print(combined.tail())

If your upstream call can return only new bars, update() still works: it deduplicates on date_column (default "date") and keeps the last row.

cache.update(
    "fold-history",
    new_bars,
    date_column="date",
    engine="polars",
)

docs.title: Manage the cache
docs.text:
cache.exists("fold-history")     # bool
cache.delete("fold-history")     # remove one file
cache.clear()                    # remove every *.parquet in the directory

get() and put() are aliases of load() and save().

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Condition Exception Unknown engine ValueError Missing date_column during update KeyError Unwritable path OSError

Note

The market functions do not write to the cache automatically. ParquetCache is a standalone building block so you stay in control of keys, retention and which symbols are persisted.

docs.title: End-to-end example
docs.text:
import iranquant as iq
from iranquant.core.cache import ParquetCache

cache = ParquetCache()

def load_or_update(symbol: str) -> object:
    key = f"{symbol}-history"
    fresh = iq.history(symbol, adjust="all", engine="polars")
    return cache.update(key, fresh, engine="polars")

history = load_or_update("فولاد")
flow = iq.compute_money_flow(history, vol_window=20)
print(flow.select(["jdate", "buyer_power_ratio"]).tail())

docs.title: Codal Reports
docs.text:
Codal report pages embed their tables as a single JavaScript object:

<script>
  var datasource = {"sheets": [ ... ]};
</script>

iranquant extracts that object without HTML scraping, then reconstructs each visible table into a DataFrame. No BeautifulSoup, no fragile CSS selectors.

docs.title: Searching announcements
docs.text:
import iranquant as iq

# Everything for a symbol
everything = iq.codal_search("فولاد", letter_type=-1, page=1)

# Monthly activity reports (گزارش فعالیت ماهانه)
monthly = iq.monthly_reports("فولاد")

# Interim financial statements
statements = iq.financial_statements("فولاد")

print(monthly.Total, len(monthly.Letters))
letter = monthly.Letters[0]
print(letter.Title, letter.PublishDateTime)
print(letter.Url)          # absolute URL

LetterType=58 selects monthly activity reports and LetterType=6 selects interim financial statements. Every returned CodalLetter has its Url, ExcelUrl and PdfUrl resolved to absolute links.

Search parameters:

Argument Default Meaning symbol None Persian ticker filter letter_type -1 Codal letter type (58, 6, …) category -1 Codal category page 1 One-based page audited True Include audited reports not_audited True Include unaudited reports mains True Include parent-company reports childs True Include subsidiary reports

docs.title: Extracting tables from a report
docs.text:
letter = iq.monthly_reports("فولاد").Letters[0]
tables = iq.codal_report(letter)          # or a URL string

The return value is a dictionary keyed by "<sheet title> - <table title>":

for name, table in tables.items():
    print(name, table.shape)

You can also work in two explicit steps:

from iranquant.codal import extract_datasource_json, parse_codal_tables

html = "<script>var datasource = {\"sheets\": []};</script>"
datasource = extract_datasource_json(html)
tables = parse_codal_tables(datasource, engine="pandas")

docs.title: How values are cleaned
docs.text:
• Invisible cells (isVisible=false) are dropped.
  • Header rows are detected from rowType/cellGroupName hints or a text-only first row; multi-row headers are joined with " - ".
  • Persian/Arabic digits become ASCII.
  • Thousands separators (٬, ,) are removed and ٫ becomes ..
  • Accounting parentheses become negative numbers: (1,200) → -1200.0.
  • Unicode minus (−) becomes -.
  • Columns with mixed text and numbers are normalized to strings; otherwise numeric cells become float.
  • Duplicate column labels receive _2, _3, … suffixes; duplicate table keys receive " (2)", " (3)", ….

docs.title: Automated monthly sales analysis
docs.text:
iranquant ships a built-in analyzer for the standard گزارش فعالیت ماهانه - تولید و فروش table. It locates the current-month, year-to-date and prior-year blocks, prefers the final جمع row (falling back to summing جمع فروش داخلی, جمع فروش صادراتی and جمع درآمد ارائه خدمات) and computes MoM/YoY growth:

import iranquant as iq

summary = iq.monthly_sales_summary("فولاد")

print(summary["period_end"])            # "1405-07-30"
print(summary["current_month_sales"])   # million Rials
print(summary["ytd_sales"])
print(summary["prev_ytd_sales"])
print(summary["mom_change_pct"])        # from the previous monthly letter
print(summary["yoy_change_pct"])
print(summary["summary_df"])            # only the جمع/مجموع rows

monthly_sales_summary fetches both the latest report and the previous distinct monthly period, so mom_change_pct is a true month-over-month comparison rather than a within-report guess. Values are reported in million Rials, the unit printed by Codal.

If you already have tables in hand, call the pure analyzer:

tables = iq.parse_codal_report(letter)   # alias of iq.codal_report
summary = iq.analyze_monthly_sales(tables)

The analyzer accepts Pandas or Polars tables:

tables = iq.parse_codal_report(letter, engine="polars")
summary = iq.analyze_monthly_sales(tables)

docs.title: CodalSearchResponse container behavior
docs.text:
Search results are sized, iterable and indexable, expose lowercase aliases and can be exported to either dataframe engine:

reports = iq.monthly_reports("فولاد")

print(len(reports), reports.total, reports.page)
for letter in reports:
    print(letter.TracingNo, letter.Title)

latest = reports[0]
frame = reports.to_dataframe()                 # pandas
frame_pl = reports.to_dataframe("polars")     # polars

docs.title: Manual extraction
docs.text:
Because sheet and column titles vary between issuers, you can still match them defensively:

import pandas as pd
import iranquant as iq

reports = iq.monthly_reports("فولاد")
if not reports.Letters:
    raise SystemExit("no monthly reports found")

latest = reports.Letters[0]
tables = iq.codal_report(latest)

# Find the first table whose title mentions sales/production.
candidates = {
    name: frame
    for name, frame in tables.items()
    if any(word in name for word in ("فروش", "تولید", "درآمد"))
}
if not candidates:
    raise SystemExit("no sales table found in this report")

name, frame = next(iter(candidates.items()))
print("using table:", name)

# Sum every column that is fully numeric after coercion.
numeric = frame.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
totals = numeric.sum(numeric_only=True)
print(totals)

To accumulate history across months, loop over reports.Letters, parse each report and keep the total you need:

rows = []
for letter in reports.Letters:
    tables = iq.codal_report(letter)
    for name, frame in tables.items():
        if "فروش" not in name:
            continue
        numeric = frame.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
        totals = numeric.sum(numeric_only=True)
        row = {"date": letter.PublishDateTime, "letter": letter.Title, **totals.to_dict()}
        rows.append(row)

history = pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values("date")
print(history.tail())

Tip

Use engine="polars" for codal_report and parse_codal_tables when you plan to aggregate large multi-year report sets; the reconstruction and cleaning rules are identical.

docs.title: Market Data
docs.text: Everything in this page is available both synchronously (iq.history(...)) and asynchronously (await client.history(...)).

docs.title: Symbol search and insCode resolution
docs.text:
import iranquant as iq

results = iq.search("فولاد")
print(results)

code = iq.get_inscode("فولاد")      # "46348559193224090"

Search output columns:

Column Type Description ins_code str TSETMC instrument code symbol str Ticker (lVal18AFC) company_name str Full company name isin str \| None International securities code shares float Total listed shares flow int Flow id (1, 2, 4 are tradable) board str Market board code last_date datetime.date \| None Last trade date last_date_jdate str \| None Jalali last trade date

Resolution details:

  • Text is normalized for Arabic yeh/kaf variants, Persian digits and zero-width characters.
  • Instruments with an active flow (1, 2, 4) win; ties go to the newest lastDate.
  • A numeric insCode (or all-digit string) bypasses the network entirely: iq.get_inscode(46348559193224090) returns immediately.
  • Both the search and resolution caches are process-local.
from iranquant.market.symbol import clear_cache
clear_cache()   # useful in long-running workers and tests

docs.title: Daily OHLCV history
docs.text:
daily = iq.history("فولاد", adjust="all")

Output columns (sorted ascending by date):

Column Type TSETMC source Notes date datetime.date dEven Gregorian jdate str dEven Jalali YYYY-MM-DD open float priceFirst high float priceMax low float priceMin close float pDrCotVal Last traded price final_price float pClosing Official closing price prev_price float priceYesterday Unadjusted previous close volume float qTotTran5J Shares value float qTotCap Rials trades float zTotTran Trade count

Sentinel dates (dEven < 19000101) and zero-volume/zero-trade placeholder rows are dropped automatically.

docs.title: Client-type (retail vs institutional) history
docs.text:
clients = iq.client_type("فولاد")
Column Type Description date datetime.date Trading date jdate str Jalali date buy_I_Volume float Retail buy volume buy_N_Volume float Institutional buy volume buy_I_Value float Retail buy value (Rials) buy_N_Value float Institutional buy value (Rials) buy_N_Count int Institutional buy orders buy_I_Count int Retail buy orders sell_I_Volume float Retail sell volume sell_N_Volume float Institutional sell volume sell_I_Value float Retail sell value (Rials) sell_N_Value float Institutional sell value (Rials) sell_N_Count int Institutional sell orders sell_I_Count int Retail sell orders

iq.full_history("فولاد") performs an outer join on date between the OHLCV frame and this client-type frame, so the result contains all eleven OHLCV columns followed by the twelve client-type columns above.

docs.title: Backward price adjustment
docs.text:
Price gaps occur on ex-dividend and capital-increase days: the raw final_price collapses while prev_price on the next day already reflects the event. The library supports three modes:

adjust Behavior "none" Raw TSETMC prices "all" Backward gap-ratio adjustment for dividends and capital increases "capital_only" Backward adjustment for capital increases only

docs.title: adjust="all" — gap ratio
docs.text:
For each day i, using the newest day as the anchor:

r[i] = prev_price[i+1] / final_price[i]
F[n-1] = 1
F[i]   = F[i+1] * r[i]

Every price column (open, high, low, close, final_price, prev_price) is multiplied by F[i], so the newest bar stays untouched and all older prices are pulled back onto today's scale.

raw = iq.history("فولاد", adjust="none")
adj = iq.history("فولاد", adjust="all")

docs.title: adjust="capital_only" — ex-rights ratio
docs.text:
For every capital increase from numberOfShareOld to numberOfShareNew, rows strictly before the event date are multiplied by:

factor = numberOfShareOld / numberOfShareNew

Rows on or after the event date are unchanged. This mode fetches the instrument's share-change history in a second request.

capital_adj = iq.history("فولاد", adjust="capital_only")

Note

apply_gap_adjustment and apply_capital_adjustment are pure functions and never mutate their input, so they can be tested in isolation or reused on custom records.

docs.title: Live MarketWatch
docs.text:
One request returns the entire market:

market = iq.market_watch()
Column Type Description ins_code str Instrument code symbol str Ticker company_name str Company name eps float \| None Earnings per share pe float \| None Price-to-earnings ratio open / high / low float Session prices close float Last traded price final_price float Closing price prev_price float Previous close volume / value / trades float Session activity tmax / tmin float Daily high/low limit total_shares float Listed shares order_book list[dict] Levels with n, qmd, zmd, pmd, pmo, zmo, qmo

The endpoint is requested verbatim (brackets in paperTypes[0]=1 are never percent-encoded). Current servers send qtj/pMax/pMin; older payloads used qtt/ps/pi and are still supported.

docs.title: Order book (BestLimits)
docs.text:
book = iq.order_book("فولاد")
Column Type Meaning n int Level (1 = best) qmd float Bid order count zmd float Bid volume pmd float Bid price pmo float Ask price zmo float Ask volume qmo float Ask order count

docs.title: Intraday candles
docs.text:
bars = iq.intraday_trades("فولاد")
Column Type Description time datetime.time \| None Bar time from hEven open / high / low / close float OHLC volume float Volume in the bar

docs.title: Indices
docs.text:
live = iq.indices_live()
overall = iq.index_history()                       # شاخص کل
equal = iq.index_history("43685683301327984")      # شاخص هم‌وزن

Standardized columns:

Column Type Description index_code str TSETMC index code name str Index name index_value float \| None Current value change float \| None Absolute change change_pct float \| None Percentage change date / jdate date/str or None Reported date time datetime.time \| None Last update

Overall and equal-weight rows also expose market_state and market_state_title. Sector rows retain every raw upstream field alongside the standardized ones. Live snapshots run the overview and sector requests concurrently; if only one succeeds, the partial result is returned.

docs.title: Quant Analytics
docs.text:
All functions accept either a Pandas or Polars frame and return the same engine type. They do not mutate their input.

import iranquant as iq
from iranquant import (
    compute_money_flow,
    compute_movement_power,
    detect_swing_legs,
    MarketScreener,
)

docs.title: Money flow and smart money
docs.text:
One callLower level 
flow = iq.money_flow("فولاد")          # fetches full_history + computes

full = iq.full_history("فولاد")
flow = compute_money_flow(full, vol_window=20)

docs.title: Required input columns
docs.text: compute_money_flow expects final_price, close, volume, buy_I_Volume, sell_I_Volume, buy_I_Count and sell_I_Count — all present in full_history.

docs.title: Exact formulas
docs.text:
real_buy_per_capita  = buy_I_Volume  * final_price / max(buy_I_Count, 1)
real_sell_per_capita = sell_I_Volume * final_price / max(sell_I_Count, 1)
buyer_power_ratio    = real_buy_per_capita / max(real_sell_per_capita, 1)

net_real_value       = (buy_I_Volume - sell_I_Volume) * final_price
ownership_change_pct = ((buy_I_Volume - sell_I_Volume) / max(volume, 1)) * 100
close_vs_final_pct   = ((close - final_price) / max(final_price, 1)) * 100
vol_ratio            = volume / rolling_mean(volume, vol_window)   # min_periods=1

*_m columns are the per-capita values expressed in million Tomans (divided by 1e7); the base *_per_capita columns are in Rials.

docs.title: Signals
docs.text:
smart_money_entry = vol_ratio >= 1.8
                    and buyer_power_ratio >= 1.5
                    and net_real_value > 0
                    and close >= final_price

smart_money_exit  = vol_ratio >= 1.8
                    and buyer_power_ratio <= 0.67
                    and net_real_value < 0
                    and close <= final_price

docs.title: Output columns
docs.text:
Column Type Meaning real_buy_per_capita float Rials per retail buy order real_buy_per_capita_m float Million Tomans per retail buy order real_sell_per_capita float Rials per retail sell order real_sell_per_capita_m float Million Tomans per retail sell order buyer_power_ratio float Real buy/sell power net_real_value float Net real money flow (Rials) ownership_change_pct float Net real volume / total volume close_vs_final_pct float Last price vs closing price vol_ratio float Volume vs rolling mean smart_money_entry bool Accumulation signal smart_money_exit bool Distribution signal 
import polars as pl

flow = iq.money_flow("فولاد", engine="polars")
entries = flow.filter(pl.col("smart_money_entry"))
print(entries.select(["jdate", "buyer_power_ratio", "net_real_value"]))

docs.title: Multi-timeframe movement power
docs.text:
power = iq.movement_power("فولاد", windows=(5, 20, 60))
# or
power = compute_movement_power(iq.full_history("فولاد"), windows=(5, 20, 60))

docs.title: Formula
docs.text:
For each window w:

er_w = sign(close - close.shift(w))
       * abs(close - close.shift(w))
       / rolling_sum(abs(close.diff()), w)

With exactly three windows the weights are (0.5, 0.3, 0.2); otherwise the window ratios are equally weighted. The weighted score is modulated by:

volume_factor = clip(volume / rolling_mean(volume, min(windows)), 0.5, 2.0)
buyer_factor  = clip(clip(buyer_power_ratio, 0.5, 3.0) / 1.5, 0.5, 1.5)

movement_power_score = clip(weighted_score * 100 * volume_factor * buyer_factor,
                            -100, +100)

buyer_power_ratio is optional; when absent the buyer factor is 1.0. The result is therefore negative for sustained down moves and positive for sustained up moves, with more efficient (straighter) moves scoring higher.

docs.title: Output columns
docs.text:
• er_<window> — signed efficiency ratio per window (for example er_5, er_20, er_60).
  • movement_power_score — final score in [-100, +100].
print(power[["jdate", "er_5", "er_20", "er_60",
             "movement_power_score"]].tail())

docs.title: ZigZag swing legs
docs.text:
legs = detect_swing_legs(iq.history("فولاد"), reversal_pct=5.0)

A swing leg is confirmed when price reverses by at least reversal_pct from the running extreme. The final, still-active leg is included, so the output always ends at the latest bar.

docs.title: Output columns
docs.text:
Column Type Meaning leg_id int One-based leg number direction int 1 up, -1 down start_date / end_date from date (or positional int) Leg bounds start_price / end_price float Pivot prices leg_return_pct float Percentage move leg_bars int Bars spanned leg_velocity float leg_return_pct / max(leg_bars, 1) avg_volume float Mean volume over the leg leg_volume_expansion float Leg average / previous leg average

leg_volume_expansion is NaN for the first leg and when the previous leg's average volume is zero.

fast_up_legs = legs[
    (legs["direction"] == 1)
    & (legs["leg_velocity"] > 0)
    & (legs["leg_volume_expansion"] > 1.5)
]
print(fast_up_legs)

docs.title: Market screener
docs.text:
market = iq.market_watch()
screener = MarketScreener(market)       # or iq.IranQuant().screener(market)
Filter Criteria filter_buy_queue() tmax > 0 and close >= tmax and buy queue volume (sum(zmd)) > 0 filter_sell_queue() tmin > 0 and close <= tmin and sell queue volume (sum(zmo)) > 0 filter_positive_tick_surge(min_diff_pct=1.5) (close - final_price) / max(final_price, 1) * 100 >= min_diff_pct scan_market(predicate) Your own Pandas DataFrame/Series predicate 
buy_locked = screener.filter_buy_queue()
sell_locked = screener.filter_sell_queue()
surges = screener.filter_positive_tick_surge(min_diff_pct=1.5)

high_volume = screener.scan_market(
    lambda df: df["volume"] > df["volume"].median()
)

Every filter returns the same engine type as the input. Each also accepts an optional alternative frame as its first argument, so one screener can be reused across several snapshots:

screener.filter_buy_queue(other_snapshot)

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Condition Exception vol_window < 1 ValueError reversal_pct <= 0 ValueError Empty/negative windows ValueError Required column missing KeyError Predicate returns neither DataFrame nor Series TypeError

docs.title: Streaming
docs.text:
MarketWatcher polls the full MarketWatch snapshot on an interval and emits structured events when a symbol's state changes. It is deliberately simple: one request per poll, a synchronous state machine, and no hidden background tasks.

import asyncio
from iranquant import MarketWatcher
from iranquant.stream import (
    BUY_QUEUE_LOCKED,
    BUY_QUEUE_BROKEN,
    SELL_QUEUE_LOCKED,
    SELL_QUEUE_BROKEN,
    VOLUME_SPIKE,
)

async def main() -> None:
    watcher = MarketWatcher()

    @watcher.on_event(BUY_QUEUE_LOCKED)
    def on_buy_lock(event):
        print("buy queue locked:", event.symbol, event.data["buy_queue_volume"])

    @watcher.on_event(VOLUME_SPIKE)
    async def on_spike(event):
        print("spike:", event.symbol, event.data["delta"])

    @watcher.on_event("*")            # wildcard: every event
    def log(event):
        print(event.event_type, event.symbol)

    async for event in watcher.watch(
        interval=3.0,
        symbols=["فولاد", "خودرو"],
        only_market_hours=True,
    ):
        print("yielded:", event.event_type, event.symbol)

asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
Constant Trigger Reset when BUY_QUEUE_LOCKED close >= tmax and buy queue volume > 0 — BUY_QUEUE_BROKEN A previously locked buy queue disappears After a BUY_QUEUE_LOCKED SELL_QUEUE_LOCKED close <= tmin and sell queue volume > 0 — SELL_QUEUE_BROKEN A previously locked sell queue disappears After a SELL_QUEUE_LOCKED VOLUME_SPIKE Per-poll volume increase >= 1.8x the running average increase —

Queue volume is the sum of zmd (bid) or zmo (ask) across all order-book levels.

docs.title: MarketEvent
docs.text:
Attribute Type Description event_type str One of the constants above ins_code str TSETMC instrument code symbol str Persian ticker timestamp datetime.datetime Detection time (UTC unless supplied) data dict Event-specific payload

Queue events carry close, tmax, tmin, buy_queue_volume, sell_queue_volume and volume. VOLUME_SPIKE carries volume, delta, avg_delta and close.

docs.title: Callbacks
docs.text:
Register callbacks with the on_event decorator. Callbacks may be plain functions or async def; awaitable results are awaited automatically. Type-specific listeners run before wildcard ("*") listeners.

@watcher.on_event(VOLUME_SPIKE)
async def on_spike(event):
    await notify(event.symbol, event.data["delta"])

You can also dispatch manually:

events = watcher.process_snapshot(snapshot, symbols=["فولاد"])
await watcher.dispatch(events)

docs.title: Backtesting without the network
docs.text:
process_snapshot is synchronous and stateful, so you can feed it historical snapshots to reproduce events deterministically:

watcher = MarketWatcher()

for snapshot in historical_snapshots:          # each a MarketWatch-style frame
    events = watcher.process_snapshot(snapshot)
    for event in events:
        print(event.timestamp, event.event_type, event.symbol)

watcher.reset()                                # start a new session

reset() forgets per-symbol state but keeps registered listeners.

docs.title: Using a shared client
docs.text:
MarketWatcher accepts an existing AsyncHTTPClient, which it will not close. This is what AsyncIranQuant.watch() does:

import asyncio
import iranquant as iq

async def main() -> None:
    async with iq.AsyncIranQuant() as client:
        async for event in client.watch(interval=5.0, symbols=["فولاد"]):
            print(event.event_type, event.symbol)

asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: Market hours
docs.text:
is_market_open() returns True on Saturday–Wednesday, 09:00–12:30 Tehran time (inclusive), using Asia/Tehran with a fixed +03:30 fallback when tzdata is unavailable.

from iranquant import is_market_open

if not is_market_open():
    print("market closed")

With only_market_hours=True, the watcher sleeps through closed periods instead of polling.

docs.title: Error behavior
docs.text:
• Network and parse errors during a poll are swallowed; the watcher sleeps and retries on the next interval.
  • interval <= 0 raises ValueError when iteration starts.
  • Cancelling the async iterator closes a watcher-owned client automatically.

docs.text:
AsyncHTTPClient(
    *,
    timeout: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT,
    max_concurrency: int = MAX_CONCURRENCY,
    max_retries: int = MAX_RETRIES,
    retry_wait: float = RETRY_WAIT,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    proxy: str | None = None,
    trust_env: bool | None = None,
)

Small retrying wrapper around :class:httpx.AsyncClient.

Three transports are maintained:

  • a regular verified client used for TSETMC;
  • an insecure client used for every *.codal.ir domain, whose certificate chains frequently fail strict verification;
  • an insecure HTTP/1.1 fallback used once for TSETMC when the primary connection fails with an SSL/proxy-style error.

Environment proxy variables are ignored by default (trust_env=False) to avoid corporate/VPN HTTP proxies breaking direct connections to domestic Iranian hosts. Pass proxy=... to opt into an explicit proxy.

Create the pooled HTTP transports.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default timeout float

Per-request timeout in seconds. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT (30 s).

DEFAULT_TIMEOUT max_concurrency int

Maximum number of simultaneous requests enforced by an internal :class:asyncio.Semaphore. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.MAX_CONCURRENCY (10).

MAX_CONCURRENCY max_retries int

Total attempts per request. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.MAX_RETRIES (3).

MAX_RETRIES retry_wait float

Base wait used by the exponential retry backoff, in seconds. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.RETRY_WAIT (0.5).

RETRY_WAIT headers Mapping[str, str] | None

Extra headers merged over the built-in TSETMC/Codal headers.

None proxy str | None

Optional explicit proxy URL, e.g. "http://127.0.0.1:9090". When omitted, environment proxy variables are ignored.

None trust_env bool | None

Whether to honour HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY and other environment settings. Defaults to True only when an explicit proxy is supplied, otherwise False.

None

Examples:

>>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(timeout=10.0, max_concurrency=5)
>>> client.trust_env
False
>>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(proxy="http://127.0.0.1:9090")
>>> client.trust_env
True

def __init__(
    self,
    *,
    timeout: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT,
    max_concurrency: int = MAX_CONCURRENCY,
    max_retries: int = MAX_RETRIES,
    retry_wait: float = RETRY_WAIT,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    proxy: str | None = None,
    trust_env: bool | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Create the pooled HTTP transports.

    Args:
        timeout: Per-request timeout in seconds.  Defaults to
            :data:`iranquant.config.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT` (30 s).
        max_concurrency: Maximum number of simultaneous requests enforced
            by an internal :class:`asyncio.Semaphore`.  Defaults to
            :data:`iranquant.config.MAX_CONCURRENCY` (10).
        max_retries: Total attempts per request.  Defaults to
            :data:`iranquant.config.MAX_RETRIES` (3).
        retry_wait: Base wait used by the exponential retry backoff, in
            seconds.  Defaults to :data:`iranquant.config.RETRY_WAIT` (0.5).
        headers: Extra headers merged over the built-in TSETMC/Codal
            headers.
        proxy: Optional explicit proxy URL, e.g.
            ``"http://127.0.0.1:9090"``.  When omitted, environment proxy
            variables are ignored.
        trust_env: Whether to honour ``HTTP_PROXY`` / ``HTTPS_PROXY`` and
            other environment settings.  Defaults to ``True`` only when an
            explicit ``proxy`` is supplied, otherwise ``False``.

    Examples:
        >>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(timeout=10.0, max_concurrency=5)
        >>> client.trust_env
        False
        >>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(proxy="http://127.0.0.1:9090")
        >>> client.trust_env
        True
    """
    self._semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(max_concurrency)
    self._max_retries = max_retries
    self._retry_wait = retry_wait
    self._headers = dict(headers or {})
    self.proxy = proxy
    # Explicit proxies imply honouring the environment unless overridden.
    self.trust_env = (proxy is not None) if trust_env is None else trust_env

    common: dict[str, Any] = {
        "timeout": timeout,
        "follow_redirects": True,
        "trust_env": self.trust_env,
        "http2": False,
    }
    if proxy is not None:
        common["proxy"] = proxy

    self._client = httpx.AsyncClient(
        headers={**TSETMC_HEADERS, **self._headers},
        **common,
    )
    # Dedicated insecure transport for Codal (SSL chain bugs).
    self._codal_client = httpx.AsyncClient(
        headers={**CODAL_HEADERS, **self._headers},
        verify=False,
        **common,
    )
    # Last-resort HTTP/1.1 + no-verify transport for TSETMC.
    self._fallback_client = httpx.AsyncClient(
        headers={**TSETMC_HEADERS, **self._headers},
        verify=False,
        **common,
    )

Perform a GET request with retries and TLS fallbacks.

The request is retried up to max_retries times on network errors, and responses with status codes >= 500 are treated as retryable. A TSETMC connection that fails with SSLError/ConnectError is retried once over an insecure HTTP/1.1 transport. Every *.codal.ir request uses the dedicated certificate-relaxed transport.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default url str

Absolute request URL.

required params Mapping[str, Any] | None

Optional query parameters. Ignored for URL encoding when raw is true.

None headers Mapping[str, str] | None

Optional per-request headers merged over the defaults.

None raw bool

When true the URL string is sent verbatim without percent-encoding. Required for the MarketWatch endpoint, whose paperTypes[0]=1 brackets must stay literal.

False

Returns:

Type Description Response

The successful :class:httpx.Response.

Raises:

Type Description NetworkError

If the host is unreachable, a non-2xx status is returned, or all retries are exhausted.

Examples:

>>> response = await client.get("https://cdn.tsetmc.com/api/BestLimits/1")
>>> response.status_code
200
Source code in src/iranquant/core/client.py 
async def get(
    self,
    url: str,
    *,
    params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    raw: bool = False,
) -> httpx.Response:
    """Perform a GET request with retries and TLS fallbacks.

    The request is retried up to ``max_retries`` times on network errors,
    and responses with status codes >= 500 are treated as retryable.  A
    TSETMC connection that fails with ``SSLError``/``ConnectError`` is
    retried once over an insecure HTTP/1.1 transport.  Every ``*.codal.ir``
    request uses the dedicated certificate-relaxed transport.

    Args:
        url: Absolute request URL.
        params: Optional query parameters.  Ignored for URL encoding when
            ``raw`` is true.
        headers: Optional per-request headers merged over the defaults.
        raw: When true the URL string is sent verbatim without
            percent-encoding.  Required for the MarketWatch endpoint, whose
            ``paperTypes[0]=1`` brackets must stay literal.

    Returns:
        The successful :class:`httpx.Response`.

    Raises:
        NetworkError: If the host is unreachable, a non-2xx status is
            returned, or all retries are exhausted.

    Examples:
        >>> response = await client.get("https://cdn.tsetmc.com/api/BestLimits/1")
        >>> response.status_code
        200
    """

    target = self._build_url(url, params, raw=raw)

    try:
        async for attempt in self._retrying():
            with attempt:
                response = await self._send_with_fallback(target, headers)
                if response.status_code >= 500:
                    raise NetworkError(f"Server error {response.status_code} for {target}")
                response.raise_for_status()
                return response
    except httpx.HTTPStatusError as exc:
        raise NetworkError(f"HTTP {exc.response.status_code} for {exc.request.url}") from exc
    except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
        raise NetworkError(f"Request failed for {target}: {exc}") from exc

    raise NetworkError(f"Request failed after retries: {target}")

async def get_json(
    self,
    url: str,
    *,
    params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    raw: bool = False,
) -> Any:
    """GET a URL and decode its JSON body.

    Args:
        url: Absolute request URL.
        params: Optional query parameters.
        headers: Optional per-request headers.
        raw: When true, send the URL untouched (see :meth:`get`).

    Returns:
        The decoded JSON value (usually a ``dict`` or ``list``).

    Raises:
        NetworkError: If the request fails after retries.
        ParseError: If the response body is not valid JSON.

    Examples:
        >>> payload = await client.get_json(
        ...     "https://cdn.tsetmc.com/api/Instrument/GetInstrumentSearch/فولاد"
        ... )
        >>> "instrumentSearch" in payload
        True
    """

    response = await self.get(url, params=params, headers=headers, raw=raw)
    try:
        return response.json()
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise ParseError(f"Invalid JSON from {response.request.url}") from exc

async def aclose(self) -> None:
    """Close the primary, Codal and fallback HTTP transports.

    Safe to call more than once.  After closing, the instance must not be
    used again.

    Examples:
        >>> client = AsyncHTTPClient()
        >>> await client.aclose()
    """
    await self._client.aclose()
    await self._codal_client.aclose()
    await self._fallback_client.aclose()

def to_dataframe(
    self,
    engine: Literal["pandas", "polars"] = "pandas",
) -> Any:
    """Export the letters to a Pandas or Polars DataFrame.

    Args:
        engine: ``"pandas"`` (default) or ``"polars"``.

    Returns:
        One row per letter with the declared :class:`CodalLetter` fields as
        columns (including nested extra fields is intentionally avoided so
        the schema stays stable).

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``engine`` is unsupported.

    Examples:
        >>> frame = iq.monthly_reports("فولاد").to_dataframe()
        >>> frame[["Symbol", "TracingNo", "Title"]].head()
    """

    columns = list(CodalLetter.model_fields)
    records = [letter.model_dump(include=set(columns)) for letter in self.Letters]
    if engine == "pandas":
        import pandas as pd

        return pd.DataFrame(records, columns=columns)
    if engine == "polars":
        import polars as pl

        if not records:
            return pl.DataFrame({column: [] for column in columns})
        return pl.DataFrame(records)
    raise ValueError(f"Unsupported dataframe engine: {engine!r}")

>>> resolve_codal_url("/Report/123")

Source code in src/iranquant/codal/search.py 
def resolve_codal_url(url: str) -> str:
    """Make a Codal link absolute (``/foo`` -> ``https://codal.ir/foo``).

    Protocol-relative links (``//cdn...``) become HTTPS, root-relative links
    are prefixed with :data:`iranquant.config.CODAL_BASE`, and absolute URLs
    are returned unchanged.  Empty strings stay empty.

    Args:
        url: A raw Codal URL as returned by the search API.

    Returns:
        An absolute URL suitable for :class:`httpx.AsyncClient`.

    Examples:
        >>> resolve_codal_url("/Report/123")
        'https://codal.ir/Report/123'
        >>> resolve_codal_url("//cdn.codal.ir/a.pdf")
        'https://cdn.codal.ir/a.pdf'
    """

    cleaned = url.strip()
    if not cleaned:
        return cleaned
    if cleaned.startswith("//"):
        return f"https:{cleaned}"
    if cleaned.startswith("/"):
        return f"{CODAL_BASE}{cleaned}"
    if cleaned.startswith("http://") or cleaned.startswith("https://"):
        return cleaned
    return f"{CODAL_BASE}/{cleaned.lstrip('/')}"

def _resolve_letter_urls(letter: CodalLetter) -> CodalLetter:
    letter.Url = resolve_codal_url(letter.Url)
    if letter.ExcelUrl:

async def _search(
    client: AsyncHTTPClient,
    *,
    symbol: str | None,
    letter_type: int,
    category: int,
    page: int,
    audited: bool,
    not_audited: bool,
    mains: bool,
    childs: bool,
) -> CodalSearchResponse:
    params: dict[str, Any] = {
        "Symbol": symbol or "",
        "LetterType": letter_type,
        "Category": category,
        "CompanyState": -1,
        "CompanyType": -1,
        "PageNumber": page,
        "Audited": str(audited).lower(),
        "NotAudited": str(not_audited).lower(),
        "Mains": str(mains).lower(),
        "Childs": str(childs).lower(),
        "Consolidatable": "true",
        "NotConsolidatable": "true",
        "Publisher": "false",
        "search": "true",
    }
    payload = await client.get_json(CODAL_SEARCH_URL, params=params)
    try:
        response = CodalSearchResponse.model_validate(payload)
    except Exception as exc:  # pydantic.ValidationError
        raise ParseError("Unexpected Codal search payload") from exc

    response.Letters = [_resolve_letter_urls(letter) for letter in response.Letters]
    return response

async def search_codal(
    symbol: str | None = None,
    letter_type: int = -1,
    category: int = -1,
    page: int = 1,
    audited: bool = True,
    not_audited: bool = True,
    mains: bool = True,
    childs: bool = True,
    *,
    client: AsyncHTTPClient | None = None,
) -> CodalSearchResponse:
    """Search Codal announcements.

    Parameters mirror the ``search.codal.ir`` query API.  A temporary client is
    created and closed when ``client`` is not supplied.  Every returned letter
    has its ``Url``, ``ExcelUrl`` and ``PdfUrl`` resolved to absolute URLs.

    Args:
        symbol: Optional Persian ticker to filter by, e.g. ``"فولاد"``.
        letter_type: Codal ``LetterType`` filter.  ``-1`` means all types;
            ``58`` selects monthly activity reports and ``6`` selects interim
            financial statements.  Defaults to ``-1``.
        category: Codal ``Category`` filter; ``-1`` means all.  Defaults to
            ``-1``.
        page: One-based result page.  Defaults to ``1``.
        audited: Include audited reports.  Defaults to ``True``.
        not_audited: Include unaudited reports.  Defaults to ``True``.
        mains: Include parent-company reports.  Defaults to ``True``.
        childs: Include subsidiary reports.  Defaults to ``True``.
        client: Optional shared :class:`~iranquant.core.client.AsyncHTTPClient`.
            When omitted a temporary client is used and closed.

    Returns:
        A :class:`~iranquant.models.codal.CodalSearchResponse` with ``Total``,
        ``Page`` and a list of :class:`~iranquant.models.codal.CodalLetter`.

    Raises:
        NetworkError: If ``search.codal.ir`` cannot be reached.
        ParseError: If the response is not valid JSON or does not match the
            expected schema.

    Examples:
        >>> response = await search_codal("فولاد", letter_type=58)
        >>> response.Total
        12
        >>> response.Letters[0].Url.startswith("https://codal.ir")
        True
    """

    if client is not None:
        return await _search(
            client,
            symbol=symbol,
            letter_type=letter_type,
            category=category,
            page=page,
            audited=audited,
            not_audited=not_audited,
            mains=mains,
            childs=childs,
        )

    http = AsyncHTTPClient()
    try:
        return await _search(
            http,
            symbol=symbol,
            letter_type=letter_type,
            category=category,
            page=page,
            audited=audited,
            not_audited=not_audited,
            mains=mains,
            childs=childs,
        )
    finally:
        await http.aclose()

AsyncHTTPClient(
    *,
    timeout: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT,
    max_concurrency: int = MAX_CONCURRENCY,
    max_retries: int = MAX_RETRIES,
    retry_wait: float = RETRY_WAIT,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    proxy: str | None = None,
    trust_env: bool | None = None,
)

Small retrying wrapper around :class:httpx.AsyncClient.

Three transports are maintained:

  • a regular verified client used for TSETMC;
  • an insecure client used for every *.codal.ir domain, whose certificate chains frequently fail strict verification;
  • an insecure HTTP/1.1 fallback used once for TSETMC when the primary connection fails with an SSL/proxy-style error.

Environment proxy variables are ignored by default (trust_env=False) to avoid corporate/VPN HTTP proxies breaking direct connections to domestic Iranian hosts. Pass proxy=... to opt into an explicit proxy.

Create the pooled HTTP transports.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default timeout float

Per-request timeout in seconds. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT (30 s).

DEFAULT_TIMEOUT max_concurrency int

Maximum number of simultaneous requests enforced by an internal :class:asyncio.Semaphore. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.MAX_CONCURRENCY (10).

MAX_CONCURRENCY max_retries int

Total attempts per request. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.MAX_RETRIES (3).

MAX_RETRIES retry_wait float

Base wait used by the exponential retry backoff, in seconds. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.RETRY_WAIT (0.5).

RETRY_WAIT headers Mapping[str, str] | None

Extra headers merged over the built-in TSETMC/Codal headers.

None proxy str | None

Optional explicit proxy URL, e.g. "http://127.0.0.1:9090". When omitted, environment proxy variables are ignored.

None trust_env bool | None

Whether to honour HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY and other environment settings. Defaults to True only when an explicit proxy is supplied, otherwise False.

None

Examples:

>>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(timeout=10.0, max_concurrency=5)
>>> client.trust_env
False
>>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(proxy="http://127.0.0.1:9090")
>>> client.trust_env
True

def __init__(
    self,
    *,
    timeout: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT,
    max_concurrency: int = MAX_CONCURRENCY,
    max_retries: int = MAX_RETRIES,
    retry_wait: float = RETRY_WAIT,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    proxy: str | None = None,
    trust_env: bool | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Create the pooled HTTP transports.

    Args:
        timeout: Per-request timeout in seconds.  Defaults to
            :data:`iranquant.config.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT` (30 s).
        max_concurrency: Maximum number of simultaneous requests enforced
            by an internal :class:`asyncio.Semaphore`.  Defaults to
            :data:`iranquant.config.MAX_CONCURRENCY` (10).
        max_retries: Total attempts per request.  Defaults to
            :data:`iranquant.config.MAX_RETRIES` (3).
        retry_wait: Base wait used by the exponential retry backoff, in
            seconds.  Defaults to :data:`iranquant.config.RETRY_WAIT` (0.5).
        headers: Extra headers merged over the built-in TSETMC/Codal
            headers.
        proxy: Optional explicit proxy URL, e.g.
            ``"http://127.0.0.1:9090"``.  When omitted, environment proxy
            variables are ignored.
        trust_env: Whether to honour ``HTTP_PROXY`` / ``HTTPS_PROXY`` and
            other environment settings.  Defaults to ``True`` only when an
            explicit ``proxy`` is supplied, otherwise ``False``.

    Examples:
        >>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(timeout=10.0, max_concurrency=5)
        >>> client.trust_env
        False
        >>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(proxy="http://127.0.0.1:9090")
        >>> client.trust_env
        True
    """
    self._semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(max_concurrency)
    self._max_retries = max_retries
    self._retry_wait = retry_wait
    self._headers = dict(headers or {})
    self.proxy = proxy
    # Explicit proxies imply honouring the environment unless overridden.
    self.trust_env = (proxy is not None) if trust_env is None else trust_env

    common: dict[str, Any] = {
        "timeout": timeout,
        "follow_redirects": True,
        "trust_env": self.trust_env,
        "http2": False,
    }
    if proxy is not None:
        common["proxy"] = proxy

    self._client = httpx.AsyncClient(
        headers={**TSETMC_HEADERS, **self._headers},
        **common,
    )
    # Dedicated insecure transport for Codal (SSL chain bugs).
    self._codal_client = httpx.AsyncClient(
        headers={**CODAL_HEADERS, **self._headers},
        verify=False,
        **common,
    )
    # Last-resort HTTP/1.1 + no-verify transport for TSETMC.
    self._fallback_client = httpx.AsyncClient(
        headers={**TSETMC_HEADERS, **self._headers},
        verify=False,
        **common,
    )

The request is retried up to max_retries times on network errors, and responses with status codes >= 500 are treated as retryable. A TSETMC connection that fails with SSLError/ConnectError is retried once over an insecure HTTP/1.1 transport. Every *.codal.ir request uses the dedicated certificate-relaxed transport.

Source code in src/iranquant/core/client.py 
async def get(
    self,
    url: str,
    *,
    params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    raw: bool = False,
) -> httpx.Response:
    """Perform a GET request with retries and TLS fallbacks.

    The request is retried up to ``max_retries`` times on network errors,
    and responses with status codes >= 500 are treated as retryable.  A
    TSETMC connection that fails with ``SSLError``/``ConnectError`` is
    retried once over an insecure HTTP/1.1 transport.  Every ``*.codal.ir``
    request uses the dedicated certificate-relaxed transport.

    Args:
        url: Absolute request URL.
        params: Optional query parameters.  Ignored for URL encoding when
            ``raw`` is true.
        headers: Optional per-request headers merged over the defaults.
        raw: When true the URL string is sent verbatim without
            percent-encoding.  Required for the MarketWatch endpoint, whose
            ``paperTypes[0]=1`` brackets must stay literal.

    Returns:
        The successful :class:`httpx.Response`.

    Raises:
        NetworkError: If the host is unreachable, a non-2xx status is
            returned, or all retries are exhausted.

    Examples:
        >>> response = await client.get("https://cdn.tsetmc.com/api/BestLimits/1")
        >>> response.status_code
        200
    """

    target = self._build_url(url, params, raw=raw)

    try:
        async for attempt in self._retrying():
            with attempt:
                response = await self._send_with_fallback(target, headers)
                if response.status_code >= 500:
                    raise NetworkError(f"Server error {response.status_code} for {target}")
                response.raise_for_status()
                return response
    except httpx.HTTPStatusError as exc:
        raise NetworkError(f"HTTP {exc.response.status_code} for {exc.request.url}") from exc
    except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
        raise NetworkError(f"Request failed for {target}: {exc}") from exc

    raise NetworkError(f"Request failed after retries: {target}")

Source code in src/iranquant/codal/search.py 
def resolve_codal_url(url: str) -> str:
    """Make a Codal link absolute (``/foo`` -> ``https://codal.ir/foo``).

    Protocol-relative links (``//cdn...``) become HTTPS, root-relative links
    are prefixed with :data:`iranquant.config.CODAL_BASE`, and absolute URLs
    are returned unchanged.  Empty strings stay empty.

    Args:
        url: A raw Codal URL as returned by the search API.

    Returns:
        An absolute URL suitable for :class:`httpx.AsyncClient`.

    Examples:
        >>> resolve_codal_url("/Report/123")
        'https://codal.ir/Report/123'
        >>> resolve_codal_url("//cdn.codal.ir/a.pdf")
        'https://cdn.codal.ir/a.pdf'
    """

    cleaned = url.strip()
    if not cleaned:
        return cleaned
    if cleaned.startswith("//"):
        return f"https:{cleaned}"
    if cleaned.startswith("/"):
        return f"{CODAL_BASE}{cleaned}"
    if cleaned.startswith("http://") or cleaned.startswith("https://"):
        return cleaned
    return f"{CODAL_BASE}/{cleaned.lstrip('/')}"

def normalize_persian(text: str) -> str:
    """Normalize Persian/Arabic text for reliable comparison.

    Converts Arabic yeh/kaf/teh-marbuta to their Persian equivalents, converts
    Arabic-Indic and Persian digits to ASCII digits, removes zero-width and
    directional control characters, and collapses whitespace.

    This is what makes ``"فولاد"`` written with an Arabic yeh and the same
    symbol written with a Persian yeh resolve to the same TSETMC instrument.

    Args:
        text: Any string, including Persian, Arabic-Indic or mixed text.

    Returns:
        The normalized string with single spaces and ASCII digits.

    Examples:
        >>> normalize_persian("۱۲۳")
        '123'
        >>> normalize_persian("  علي  ")
        'علی'
    """

    translated = text.translate(_CHAR_MAP).translate(_ZERO_WIDTH)
    return " ".join(translated.split())

def _extract_balanced_object(html: str) -> str | None:
    marker = _DATASOURCE_MARKER.search(html)
    if marker is None:
        return None
    start = html.find("{", marker.end())
    if start == -1:
        return None

    depth = 0
    in_string = False
    quote = ""
    escaped = False
    for index in range(start, len(html)):
        char = html[index]
        if in_string:
            if escaped:
                escaped = False
            elif char == "\\":
                escaped = True
            elif char == quote:
                in_string = False
            continue
        if char in ('"', "'"):
            in_string = True
            quote = char
        elif char == "{":
            depth += 1
        elif char == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0:
                return html[start : index + 1]
    return None

def extract_datasource_json(html: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Extract the ``var datasource = {...}`` JSON object from a report page.

    A fast regex is tried first; if the JSON contains nested braces inside
    strings or is followed by more JavaScript, a brace-balanced scanner is used
    as a fallback.  Braces inside quoted strings are handled correctly.

    Args:
        html: The full HTML source of a Codal report page.

    Returns:
        The decoded datasource object, usually containing a ``"sheets"`` list.

    Raises:
        ParseError: If no ``var datasource`` block is found, the block is not
            valid JSON, or it decodes to something other than an object.

    Examples:
        >>> html = '<script>var datasource = {"sheets": []};</script>'
        >>> extract_datasource_json(html)
        {'sheets': []}
    """

    match = _DATASOURCE_PATTERN.search(html)
    raw = match.group(1) if match is not None else _extract_balanced_object(html)
    if raw is None:
        raise ParseError("No 'var datasource' object found in Codal report")

    try:
        parsed = json.loads(raw)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
        raise ParseError("Malformed Codal datasource JSON") from exc
    if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
        raise ParseError("Codal datasource is not a JSON object")
    return cast(dict[str, Any], parsed)

Source code in src/iranquant/codal/parser.py 
def _parse_number(value: Any) -> float | None:
    if isinstance(value, bool) or value is None:
        return None
    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):
        return float(value)
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        return None

    text = _special_to_ascii(value)
    if not text:
        return None

    negative = text.startswith("(") and text.endswith(")")
    if negative:
        text = text[1:-1].strip()

    sign = -1.0 if negative else 1.0
    if text.startswith("+") or text.startswith("-"):
        if text[0] == "-":
            sign *= -1.0
        text = text[1:].strip()

    if not _NUMBER_PATTERN.fullmatch(text):
        return None
    return sign * float(text)

    if value is None:

    if isinstance(value, bool):

def _dedupe_columns(labels: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    seen: dict[str, int] = {}
    output: list[str] = []
    for index, label in enumerate(labels):
        base = label.strip() or f"column_{index + 1}"

            seen[base] = 1
            output.append(base)
        else:
            seen[base] += 1
            output.append(f"{base}_{seen[base]}")

def _reconstruct_table(table: Any) -> tuple[list[str], list[list[Any]]]:
    raw_rows: dict[int, dict[int, Any]] = {}
    row_hints: dict[int, set[str]] = {}

    for cell in table.cells:
        if not cell.isVisible:
            continue
        row = int(cell.rowSequence or 0)
        column = int(cell.columnSequence or 0)
        raw_rows.setdefault(row, {})[column] = _clean_value(cell.value)
        for hint in (cell.rowType, cell.cellGroupName):
            if isinstance(hint, str):
                row_hints.setdefault(row, set()).add(normalize_persian(hint).lower())

    if not raw_rows:
        return [], []

    column_indexes = sorted({column for row in raw_rows.values() for column in row})
    if not column_indexes:
        return [], []

    ordered_rows: list[tuple[int, list[Any]]] = []
    for sequence in sorted(raw_rows):
        values = [raw_rows[sequence].get(column) for column in column_indexes]
        if all(value is None for value in values):
            continue
        ordered_rows.append((sequence, values))

    if not ordered_rows:
        return [], []

    header_positions: list[int] = []
    for position, (sequence, values) in enumerate(ordered_rows):
        hints = row_hints.get(sequence, set())
        hint_is_header = any(any(token in hint for token in _HEADER_HINTS) for hint in hints)
        if hint_is_header or (position == 0 and _row_looks_like_header(values)):
            header_positions.append(position)
        elif header_positions:
            # Only contiguous leading header rows are treated as headers.
            break

    header_rows = [ordered_rows[position][1] for position in header_positions]
    header_position_set = set(header_positions)
    if header_rows:
        labels: list[str] = []
        for column_index in range(len(column_indexes)):
            parts: list[str] = []
            for header_values in header_rows:
                label = _label(header_values[column_index])
                if label and (not parts or parts[-1] != label):
                    parts.append(label)
            labels.append(" - ".join(parts) if parts else f"column_{column_index + 1}")
        columns = _dedupe_columns(labels)
        data_rows = [
            values
            for position, (_, values) in enumerate(ordered_rows)
            if position not in header_position_set
        ]
    else:
        columns = _dedupe_columns([f"column_{index + 1}" for index in range(len(column_indexes))])
        data_rows = [values for _, values in ordered_rows]

    # Drop rows that became completely empty after cleaning.
    data_rows = [values for values in data_rows if any(value is not None for value in values)]
    if not data_rows:
        return columns, []

    normalized_columns = _normalize_all_columns(data_rows, len(columns))
    normalized_rows = [
        [normalized_columns[column][row] for column in range(len(columns))]
        for row in range(len(data_rows))
    ]
    return columns, normalized_rows

def _build_frame(
    columns: list[str],
    rows: list[list[Any]],

    if engine == "polars":
        if not rows:
            return pl.DataFrame({column: [] for column in columns})

def parse_codal_tables(
    datasource: dict[str, Any],
    engine: Engine = "pandas",
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Reconstruct every visible table in a Codal ``datasource`` object.

    Cells are grouped by ``rowSequence``/``columnSequence``, invisible cells are
    dropped, header rows are detected (from ``rowType``/``cellGroupName`` hints
    or a text-only first row), and multi-row headers are joined with ``" - "``.
    Persian/Arabic digits, thousands separators, ``٫`` decimals, unicode minus
    and accounting parentheses (``(1,200)`` -> ``-1200.0``) are normalized.
    Duplicate column labels get ``_2``, ``_3`` suffixes.

    Args:
        datasource: A decoded datasource object, e.g. from
            :func:`extract_datasource_json`.
        engine: ``"pandas"`` (default) or ``"polars"``.

    Returns:
        A dictionary mapping ``"<sheet title> - <table title>"`` to a clean
        DataFrame.  Persistently duplicated keys are suffixed with `` (2)``,
        `` (3)``, and so on.  Tables with no visible cells are omitted.  Values
        are numeric (``float``) when parseable, otherwise ``str``; missing
        cells are ``None``/``NaN``.

    Raises:
        ParseError: If the datasource does not match the expected structure.
        ValueError: If ``engine`` is unsupported.

    Examples:
        >>> datasource = extract_datasource_json(html)
        >>> tables = parse_codal_tables(datasource, engine="pandas")
        >>> next(iter(tables))
        'گزارش فعالیت ماهانه - تولید و فروش'
    """

    if engine not in ("pandas", "polars"):
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported dataframe engine: {engine!r}")

    try:
        model = CodalDatasource.model_validate(datasource)
    except Exception as exc:
        raise ParseError("Invalid Codal datasource structure") from exc

    output: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for sheet_index, sheet in enumerate(model.sheets):
        sheet_title = (
            normalize_persian(sheet.title_Fa or sheet.title_En or "") or f"sheet_{sheet_index + 1}"
        )
        for table_index, table in enumerate(sheet.tables):
            table_title = (
                normalize_persian(table.title_Fa or table.title_En or "")
                or f"table_{table_index + 1}"
            )
            columns, rows = _reconstruct_table(table)
            if not columns:
                continue
            key = f"{sheet_title} - {table_title}"
            if key in output:
                suffix = 2
                while f"{key} ({suffix})" in output:
                    suffix += 1
                key = f"{key} ({suffix})"
            output[key] = _build_frame(columns, rows, engine)
    return output
