async def fetch_and_parse_report(
    url_or_letter: str | CodalLetter,
    engine: Engine = "pandas",
    *,
    client: AsyncHTTPClient | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Download a Codal report page and parse all of its datasource tables.

    Relative URLs (including those on :class:`~iranquant.models.codal.CodalLetter`)
    are resolved with :func:`~iranquant.codal.search.resolve_codal_url` before
    the request is made.

    Args:
        url_or_letter: Either an absolute/relative report URL or a
            ``CodalLetter`` whose ``Url`` is used.
        engine: ``"pandas"`` (default) or ``"polars"``.
        client: Optional shared :class:`~iranquant.core.client.AsyncHTTPClient`.
            When omitted a temporary client is used and closed.

    Returns:
        The dictionary produced by :func:`parse_codal_tables`, keyed by
        ``"<sheet title> - <table title>"``.

    Raises:
        NetworkError: If the report page cannot be downloaded.
        ParseError: If the page has no valid ``var datasource`` JSON or the
            datasource structure is invalid.
        ValueError: If ``engine`` is unsupported.

    Examples:
        >>> letter = reports.Letters[0]
        >>> tables = await fetch_and_parse_report(letter)
        >>> for name, table in tables.items():
        ...     print(name, table.shape)
    """

    url = url_or_letter.Url if isinstance(url_or_letter, CodalLetter) else url_or_letter
    url = resolve_codal_url(url)

    if client is not None:
        return await _fetch_and_parse(client, url, engine)

    http = AsyncHTTPClient()
    try:
        return await _fetch_and_parse(http, url, engine)
    finally:
        await http.aclose()

Small retrying wrapper around :class:httpx.AsyncClient.

Three transports are maintained:

  • a regular verified client used for TSETMC;
  • an insecure client used for every *.codal.ir domain, whose certificate chains frequently fail strict verification;
  • an insecure HTTP/1.1 fallback used once for TSETMC when the primary connection fails with an SSL/proxy-style error.

Environment proxy variables are ignored by default (trust_env=False) to avoid corporate/VPN HTTP proxies breaking direct connections to domestic Iranian hosts. Pass proxy=... to opt into an explicit proxy.

Create the pooled HTTP transports.

Per-request timeout in seconds. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT (30 s).

DEFAULT_TIMEOUT max_concurrency int

Maximum number of simultaneous requests enforced by an internal :class:asyncio.Semaphore. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.MAX_CONCURRENCY (10).

MAX_CONCURRENCY max_retries int

Total attempts per request. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.MAX_RETRIES (3).

MAX_RETRIES retry_wait float

Base wait used by the exponential retry backoff, in seconds. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.RETRY_WAIT (0.5).

Extra headers merged over the built-in TSETMC/Codal headers.

Optional explicit proxy URL, e.g. "http://127.0.0.1:9090". When omitted, environment proxy variables are ignored.

None trust_env bool | None

Whether to honour HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY and other environment settings. Defaults to True only when an explicit proxy is supplied, otherwise False.

>>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(proxy="http://127.0.0.1:9090")

def __init__(
    self,
    *,
    timeout: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT,
    max_concurrency: int = MAX_CONCURRENCY,
    max_retries: int = MAX_RETRIES,
    retry_wait: float = RETRY_WAIT,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    proxy: str | None = None,
    trust_env: bool | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Create the pooled HTTP transports.

    Args:
        timeout: Per-request timeout in seconds.  Defaults to
            :data:`iranquant.config.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT` (30 s).
        max_concurrency: Maximum number of simultaneous requests enforced
            by an internal :class:`asyncio.Semaphore`.  Defaults to
            :data:`iranquant.config.MAX_CONCURRENCY` (10).
        max_retries: Total attempts per request.  Defaults to
            :data:`iranquant.config.MAX_RETRIES` (3).
        retry_wait: Base wait used by the exponential retry backoff, in
            seconds.  Defaults to :data:`iranquant.config.RETRY_WAIT` (0.5).
        headers: Extra headers merged over the built-in TSETMC/Codal
            headers.
        proxy: Optional explicit proxy URL, e.g.
            ``"http://127.0.0.1:9090"``.  When omitted, environment proxy
            variables are ignored.
        trust_env: Whether to honour ``HTTP_PROXY`` / ``HTTPS_PROXY`` and
            other environment settings.  Defaults to ``True`` only when an
            explicit ``proxy`` is supplied, otherwise ``False``.

    Examples:
        >>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(timeout=10.0, max_concurrency=5)
        >>> client.trust_env
        False
        >>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(proxy="http://127.0.0.1:9090")
        >>> client.trust_env
        True
    """
    self._semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(max_concurrency)
    self._max_retries = max_retries
    self._retry_wait = retry_wait
    self._headers = dict(headers or {})
    self.proxy = proxy
    # Explicit proxies imply honouring the environment unless overridden.
    self.trust_env = (proxy is not None) if trust_env is None else trust_env

    common: dict[str, Any] = {
        "timeout": timeout,
        "follow_redirects": True,
        "trust_env": self.trust_env,
        "http2": False,
    }
    if proxy is not None:
        common["proxy"] = proxy

    self._client = httpx.AsyncClient(
        headers={**TSETMC_HEADERS, **self._headers},
        **common,
    )
    # Dedicated insecure transport for Codal (SSL chain bugs).
    self._codal_client = httpx.AsyncClient(
        headers={**CODAL_HEADERS, **self._headers},
        verify=False,
        **common,
    )
    # Last-resort HTTP/1.1 + no-verify transport for TSETMC.
    self._fallback_client = httpx.AsyncClient(
        headers={**TSETMC_HEADERS, **self._headers},
        verify=False,
        **common,
    )

async def get(
    self,
    url: str,
    *,
    params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    raw: bool = False,
) -> httpx.Response:
    """Perform a GET request with retries and TLS fallbacks.

    The request is retried up to ``max_retries`` times on network errors,
    and responses with status codes >= 500 are treated as retryable.  A
    TSETMC connection that fails with ``SSLError``/``ConnectError`` is
    retried once over an insecure HTTP/1.1 transport.  Every ``*.codal.ir``
    request uses the dedicated certificate-relaxed transport.

    Args:
        url: Absolute request URL.
        params: Optional query parameters.  Ignored for URL encoding when
            ``raw`` is true.
        headers: Optional per-request headers merged over the defaults.
        raw: When true the URL string is sent verbatim without
            percent-encoding.  Required for the MarketWatch endpoint, whose
            ``paperTypes[0]=1`` brackets must stay literal.

    Returns:
        The successful :class:`httpx.Response`.

    Raises:
        NetworkError: If the host is unreachable, a non-2xx status is
            returned, or all retries are exhausted.

    Examples:
        >>> response = await client.get("https://cdn.tsetmc.com/api/BestLimits/1")
        >>> response.status_code
        200
    """

    target = self._build_url(url, params, raw=raw)

    try:
        async for attempt in self._retrying():
            with attempt:
                response = await self._send_with_fallback(target, headers)
                if response.status_code >= 500:
                    raise NetworkError(f"Server error {response.status_code} for {target}")
                response.raise_for_status()
                return response
    except httpx.HTTPStatusError as exc:
        raise NetworkError(f"HTTP {exc.response.status_code} for {exc.request.url}") from exc
    except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
        raise NetworkError(f"Request failed for {target}: {exc}") from exc

    raise NetworkError(f"Request failed after retries: {target}")

async def fetch_and_parse_report(
    url_or_letter: str | CodalLetter,
    engine: Engine = "pandas",
    *,
    client: AsyncHTTPClient | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Download a Codal report page and parse all of its datasource tables.

    Relative URLs (including those on :class:`~iranquant.models.codal.CodalLetter`)
    are resolved with :func:`~iranquant.codal.search.resolve_codal_url` before
    the request is made.

    Args:
        url_or_letter: Either an absolute/relative report URL or a
            ``CodalLetter`` whose ``Url`` is used.
        engine: ``"pandas"`` (default) or ``"polars"``.
        client: Optional shared :class:`~iranquant.core.client.AsyncHTTPClient`.
            When omitted a temporary client is used and closed.

    Returns:
        The dictionary produced by :func:`parse_codal_tables`, keyed by
        ``"<sheet title> - <table title>"``.

    Raises:
        NetworkError: If the report page cannot be downloaded.
        ParseError: If the page has no valid ``var datasource`` JSON or the
            datasource structure is invalid.
        ValueError: If ``engine`` is unsupported.

    Examples:
        >>> letter = reports.Letters[0]
        >>> tables = await fetch_and_parse_report(letter)
        >>> for name, table in tables.items():
        ...     print(name, table.shape)
    """

    url = url_or_letter.Url if isinstance(url_or_letter, CodalLetter) else url_or_letter
    url = resolve_codal_url(url)

    if client is not None:
        return await _fetch_and_parse(client, url, engine)

    http = AsyncHTTPClient()
    try:
        return await _fetch_and_parse(http, url, engine)
    finally:
        await http.aclose()

def normalize_persian(text: str) -> str:
    """Normalize Persian/Arabic text for reliable comparison.

    Converts Arabic yeh/kaf/teh-marbuta to their Persian equivalents, converts
    Arabic-Indic and Persian digits to ASCII digits, removes zero-width and
    directional control characters, and collapses whitespace.

    This is what makes ``"فولاد"`` written with an Arabic yeh and the same
    symbol written with a Persian yeh resolve to the same TSETMC instrument.

    Args:
        text: Any string, including Persian, Arabic-Indic or mixed text.

    Returns:
        The normalized string with single spaces and ASCII digits.

    Examples:
        >>> normalize_persian("۱۲۳")
        '123'
        >>> normalize_persian("  علي  ")
        'علی'
    """

    translated = text.translate(_CHAR_MAP).translate(_ZERO_WIDTH)
    return " ".join(translated.split())

def _to_number(value: Any) -> float | None:
    if _is_missing(value) or isinstance(value, bool):
        return None
    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):
        return float(value)
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        return None

    text = (
        normalize_persian(value)
        .replace("٬", "")
        .replace(",", "")
        .replace("٫", ".")
        .replace("\u2212", "-")
        .strip()
    )
    if not text or text in {"-", "—", "_"}:
        return None

    negative = text.startswith("(") and text.endswith(")")
    if negative:
        text = text[1:-1].strip()
    sign = -1.0 if negative else 1.0
    if text.startswith("+") or text.startswith("-"):
        if text[0] == "-":
            sign *= -1.0
        text = text[1:].strip()
    try:
        return sign * float(text)
    except ValueError:
        return None

def _select_table(tables: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Pick the production & sales table, falling back to the most numeric one."""

    candidates: list[tuple[float, str, pd.DataFrame]] = []
    for key, raw_frame in tables.items():
        frame = _as_pandas(raw_frame)
        if frame.empty or frame.shape[1] == 0:
            continue
        name = normalize_persian(str(key))
        score = float(_numeric_cells(frame))
        if "تولید و فروش" in name:
            score += 1_000_000.0
        elif "فروش" in name:
            score += 1_000.0
        candidates.append((score, str(key), frame))

    if not candidates:
        raise ValueError("No usable Codal tables were supplied")

    candidates.sort(key=lambda item: item[0], reverse=True)
    best = candidates[0]
    return best[1], best[2]

def _build_blocks(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> list[_Block]:
    starts: list[tuple[int, str, tuple[int, int, int] | None, bool, str]] = []
    for index, column in enumerate(frame.columns):
        label = _label(column)
        kind: str | None = None
        if any(hint in label for hint in _MONTH_HINTS) or ("دوره" in label and "ماه" in label):
            kind = "month"
        elif any(hint in label for hint in _YTD_HINTS):
            kind = "ytd"
        elif "اصلاحات" in label:
            kind = "adjustment"
        if kind is None:
            continue
        corrected = "اصلاح شده" in label or "اصلاح‌شده" in label
        starts.append((index, kind, _parse_date(label), corrected, label))

    blocks: list[_Block] = []
    for position, (start, kind, date, corrected, label) in enumerate(starts):
        end = starts[position + 1][0] if position + 1 < len(starts) else len(frame.columns)
        amount_index = end - 1
        for column_index in range(start, end):
            column_label = _label(frame.columns[column_index])
            if "مبلغ" in column_label:
                amount_index = column_index
                if "فروش" in column_label or "درآمد" in column_label:
                    break
        blocks.append(
            _Block(
                start=start,
                end=end,
                kind=kind,
                date=date,
                corrected=corrected,
                label=label,
                amount_index=amount_index,
            )
        )
    return blocks

def _pick_period_blocks(
    blocks: list[_Block],
) -> tuple[_Block | None, _Block | None, _Block | None, _Block | None]:
    """Return ``(current_month, previous_month, current_ytd, previous_ytd)``."""

    month_blocks = [block for block in blocks if block.kind == "month"]
    ytd_blocks = [block for block in blocks if block.kind == "ytd"]

    current_month: _Block | None = None
    if month_blocks:
        current_month = max(
            month_blocks,
            key=lambda block: (block.date or (0, 0, 0), block.start),
        )

    previous_month: _Block | None = None
    previous_hint = next(
        (block for block in month_blocks if any(hint in block.label for hint in _PREV_MONTH_HINTS)),
        None,
    )
    if previous_hint is not None:
        previous_month = previous_hint
    elif current_month is not None and current_month.date is not None:
        earlier = [
            block
            for block in month_blocks
            if block.date is not None and block.date < current_month.date
        ]
        if earlier:
            previous_month = max(earlier, key=lambda block: block.date or (0, 0, 0))

    report_date = max(
        (block.date for block in blocks if block.date is not None),
        default=None,
    )

    current_ytd: _Block | None = None
    previous_ytd: _Block | None = None
    if report_date is not None:
        same_period = [block for block in ytd_blocks if block.date == report_date]
        if same_period:
            current_ytd = max(
                same_period,
                key=lambda block: (not block.corrected, block.start),
            )
        earlier_year = [
            block
            for block in ytd_blocks
            if block.date is not None and block.date[0] < report_date[0]
        ]
        if earlier_year:
            previous_ytd = max(
                earlier_year,
                key=lambda block: (block.date or (0, 0, 0), block.start),
            )
    else:
        usable = [block for block in ytd_blocks if not block.corrected] or ytd_blocks
        if usable:
            current_ytd = max(usable, key=lambda block: block.start)
        previous_ytd = next(
            (
                block
                for block in ytd_blocks
                if any(hint in block.label for hint in _PRIOR_YEAR_HINTS)
            ),
            None,
        )

    return current_month, previous_month, current_ytd, previous_ytd

def _pick_total_row(labels: pd.Series) -> int | None:
    exact = labels[labels.isin(_TOTAL_LABELS)]
    if not exact.empty:
        index = int(str(exact.index[0]))
        return index

    candidates = [
        int(str(index))
        for index, label in labels.items()
        if any(token in label for token in _SUMMARY_TOKENS)
        and label not in _CATEGORY_LABELS
        and not any(hint in label for hint in _EXCLUDED_SUMMARY_HINTS)
    ]
    return candidates[-1] if candidates else None

def _aggregate(
    frame: pd.DataFrame,
    total_row: int | None,
    category_rows: list[int],
    column: int,
) -> float | None:
    if total_row is not None:
        value = _row_value(frame, total_row, column)
        if value is not None:
            return value
    values = [
        value
        for value in (_row_value(frame, row, column) for row in category_rows)
        if value is not None
    ]
    return float(sum(values)) if values else None

def analyze_monthly_sales(tables: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Summarize a monthly activity report's production & sales table.

    The main table is the one whose key contains ``"تولید و فروش"``; if no such
    key exists, the table with the most numeric cells is used.  Summary rows are
    detected by normalized ``جمع``/``مجموع`` labels.  A final ``جمع`` row is
    preferred; when it is absent, the ``جمع فروش داخلی``, ``جمع فروش صادراتی``
    and ``جمع درآمد ارائه خدمات`` rows are added together.

    Values are reported in **million Rials**, the unit printed in the source
    table.  ``prev_month_sales`` is only populated when the same table exposes a
    separate previous-month period; :func:`monthly_sales_summary` fills it by
    parsing the previous monthly letter.

    Args:
        tables: The mapping returned by
            :func:`~iranquant.codal.parser.fetch_and_parse_report` (or
            :func:`~iranquant.codal.parser.parse_codal_tables`), with Pandas or
            Polars DataFrames as values.

    Returns:
        A dictionary with:

        * ``table_key`` (``str``) — key of the selected table.
        * ``period_end`` (``str | None``) — latest reporting date in the table.
        * ``current_month_sales`` (``float | None``) — one-month sales amount.
        * ``prev_month_sales`` (``float | None``) — previous standalone month,
            when present in the same table.
        * ``ytd_sales`` (``float | None``) — year-to-date sales amount.
        * ``prev_ytd_sales`` (``float | None``) — prior-year YTD sales amount.
        * ``mom_change_pct`` (``float | None``) — month-over-month percentage.
        * ``yoy_change_pct`` (``float | None``) — year-over-year percentage.
        * ``summary_df`` (``pandas.DataFrame``) — filtered summary rows.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``tables`` is empty or contains no usable table.
        TypeError: If a table value is not a Pandas or Polars DataFrame.

    Examples:
        >>> letter = iq.monthly_reports("فولاد").Letters[0]
        >>> tables = iq.parse_codal_report(letter)
        >>> summary = iq.analyze_monthly_sales(tables)
        >>> summary["current_month_sales"]
        662639489.0
        >>> summary["summary_df"][["شرح - نام محصول"]]
    """

    table_key, frame = _select_table(tables)
    label_column = frame.columns[0]
    labels = frame[label_column].map(_label)

    summary_mask = labels.str.contains("جمع|مجموع", regex=True, na=False)
    summary_df = frame.loc[summary_mask].copy().reset_index(drop=True)

    total_row = _pick_total_row(labels)
    category_rows = [int(str(index)) for index in labels[labels.isin(_CATEGORY_LABELS)].index]

    blocks = _build_blocks(frame)
    current_month, previous_month, current_ytd, previous_ytd = _pick_period_blocks(blocks)

    current_month_sales = (
        _aggregate(frame, total_row, category_rows, current_month.amount_index)
        if current_month is not None
        else None
    )
    prev_month_sales = (
        _aggregate(frame, total_row, category_rows, previous_month.amount_index)
        if previous_month is not None
        else None
    )
    ytd_sales = (
        _aggregate(frame, total_row, category_rows, current_ytd.amount_index)
        if current_ytd is not None
        else None
    )
    prev_ytd_sales = (
        _aggregate(frame, total_row, category_rows, previous_ytd.amount_index)
        if previous_ytd is not None
        else None
    )

    period_end = None
    if current_month is not None and current_month.date is not None:
        period_end = "{:04d}-{:02d}-{:02d}".format(*current_month.date)
    elif current_ytd is not None and current_ytd.date is not None:
        period_end = "{:04d}-{:02d}-{:02d}".format(*current_ytd.date)

    return {
        "table_key": table_key,
        "period_end": period_end,
        "current_month_sales": current_month_sales,
        "prev_month_sales": prev_month_sales,
        "ytd_sales": ytd_sales,
        "prev_ytd_sales": prev_ytd_sales,
        "mom_change_pct": _pct_change(current_month_sales, prev_month_sales),
        "yoy_change_pct": _pct_change(ytd_sales, prev_ytd_sales),
        "summary_df": summary_df,
    }

async def monthly_sales_summary(
    symbol: str,
    page: int = 1,
    *,
    client: AsyncHTTPClient | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Fetch and analyze a symbol's latest monthly sales report.

    The newest report on ``page`` is parsed, and its previous distinct monthly
    period is parsed too so a true Month-over-Month comparison can be computed.

    Args:
        symbol: Persian ticker, e.g. ``"فولاد"``.
        page: One-based Codal result page.  Defaults to ``1``.
        client: Optional shared :class:`~iranquant.core.client.AsyncHTTPClient`.

    Returns:
        The dictionary from :func:`analyze_monthly_sales` plus
        ``symbol``, ``tracing_no``, ``title``, ``prev_month_tracing_no`` and a
        ``mom_change_pct`` derived from the previous month's report.

    Raises:
        ParseError: If Codal returns no HTML monthly reports.
        NetworkError: If Codal or the report page cannot be fetched.
        ValueError: If the latest report has no usable tables.

    Examples:
        >>> summary = await monthly_sales_summary("فولاد")
        >>> summary["current_month_sales"]
        >>> summary["mom_change_pct"]
    """

    reports = await get_monthly_reports(symbol, page=page, client=client)
    letters = [letter for letter in reports.Letters if letter.HasHtml and letter.Url]
    if not letters:
        raise ParseError(f"No HTML monthly report found for {symbol!r}")

    def sort_key(letter: Any) -> tuple[tuple[int, int, int], int]:
        period = _letter_period(letter) or (0, 0, 0)
        return period, int(getattr(letter, "TracingNo", 0) or 0)

    ordered = sorted(letters, key=sort_key, reverse=True)
    latest = ordered[0]
    latest_period = _letter_period(latest)

    tables = await fetch_and_parse_report(latest, client=client)
    result = analyze_monthly_sales(tables)
    result.update(
        {
            "symbol": normalize_persian(symbol),
            "tracing_no": latest.TracingNo,
            "title": latest.Title,
            "page": page,
        }
    )

    previous = next(
        (
            letter
            for letter in ordered[1:]
            if latest_period is None or (_letter_period(letter) or (0, 0, 0)) < latest_period
        ),
        None,
    )
    if previous is None:
        return result

    try:
        previous_tables = await fetch_and_parse_report(previous, client=client)
        previous_result = analyze_monthly_sales(previous_tables)
    except (IranQuantError, ValueError, TypeError):
        return result

    previous_sales = previous_result.get("current_month_sales")
    if isinstance(previous_sales, (int, float)):
        result["prev_month_sales"] = float(previous_sales)
        result["prev_month_tracing_no"] = previous.TracingNo
        current_sales = result.get("current_month_sales")
        result["mom_change_pct"] = _pct_change(
            float(current_sales) if isinstance(current_sales, (int, float)) else None,
            float(previous_sales),
        )
    return result

AsyncHTTPClient(
    *,
    timeout: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT,
    max_concurrency: int = MAX_CONCURRENCY,
    max_retries: int = MAX_RETRIES,
    retry_wait: float = RETRY_WAIT,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    proxy: str | None = None,
    trust_env: bool | None = None,

Small retrying wrapper around :class:httpx.AsyncClient.

Three transports are maintained:

  • a regular verified client used for TSETMC;
  • an insecure client used for every *.codal.ir domain, whose certificate chains frequently fail strict verification;
  • an insecure HTTP/1.1 fallback used once for TSETMC when the primary connection fails with an SSL/proxy-style error.

Environment proxy variables are ignored by default (trust_env=False) to avoid corporate/VPN HTTP proxies breaking direct connections to domestic Iranian hosts. Pass proxy=... to opt into an explicit proxy.

Create the pooled HTTP transports.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default timeout float

Per-request timeout in seconds. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT (30 s).

DEFAULT_TIMEOUT max_concurrency int

Maximum number of simultaneous requests enforced by an internal :class:asyncio.Semaphore. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.MAX_CONCURRENCY (10).

MAX_CONCURRENCY max_retries int

Total attempts per request. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.MAX_RETRIES (3).

MAX_RETRIES retry_wait float

Base wait used by the exponential retry backoff, in seconds. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.RETRY_WAIT (0.5).

RETRY_WAIT headers Mapping[str, str] | None

Extra headers merged over the built-in TSETMC/Codal headers.

None proxy str | None

Optional explicit proxy URL, e.g. "http://127.0.0.1:9090". When omitted, environment proxy variables are ignored.

None trust_env bool | None

Whether to honour HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY and other environment settings. Defaults to True only when an explicit proxy is supplied, otherwise False.

None

Examples:

>>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(timeout=10.0, max_concurrency=5)
>>> client.trust_env
False
>>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(proxy="http://127.0.0.1:9090")
>>> client.trust_env

def __init__(
    self,
    *,
    timeout: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT,
    max_concurrency: int = MAX_CONCURRENCY,
    max_retries: int = MAX_RETRIES,
    retry_wait: float = RETRY_WAIT,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    proxy: str | None = None,
    trust_env: bool | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Create the pooled HTTP transports.

    Args:
        timeout: Per-request timeout in seconds.  Defaults to
            :data:`iranquant.config.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT` (30 s).
        max_concurrency: Maximum number of simultaneous requests enforced
            by an internal :class:`asyncio.Semaphore`.  Defaults to
            :data:`iranquant.config.MAX_CONCURRENCY` (10).
        max_retries: Total attempts per request.  Defaults to
            :data:`iranquant.config.MAX_RETRIES` (3).
        retry_wait: Base wait used by the exponential retry backoff, in
            seconds.  Defaults to :data:`iranquant.config.RETRY_WAIT` (0.5).
        headers: Extra headers merged over the built-in TSETMC/Codal
            headers.
        proxy: Optional explicit proxy URL, e.g.
            ``"http://127.0.0.1:9090"``.  When omitted, environment proxy
            variables are ignored.
        trust_env: Whether to honour ``HTTP_PROXY`` / ``HTTPS_PROXY`` and
            other environment settings.  Defaults to ``True`` only when an
            explicit ``proxy`` is supplied, otherwise ``False``.

    Examples:
        >>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(timeout=10.0, max_concurrency=5)
        >>> client.trust_env
        False
        >>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(proxy="http://127.0.0.1:9090")
        >>> client.trust_env
        True
    """
    self._semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(max_concurrency)
    self._max_retries = max_retries
    self._retry_wait = retry_wait
    self._headers = dict(headers or {})
    self.proxy = proxy
    # Explicit proxies imply honouring the environment unless overridden.
    self.trust_env = (proxy is not None) if trust_env is None else trust_env

    common: dict[str, Any] = {
        "timeout": timeout,
        "follow_redirects": True,
        "trust_env": self.trust_env,
        "http2": False,
    }
    if proxy is not None:
        common["proxy"] = proxy

    self._client = httpx.AsyncClient(
        headers={**TSETMC_HEADERS, **self._headers},
        **common,
    )
    # Dedicated insecure transport for Codal (SSL chain bugs).
    self._codal_client = httpx.AsyncClient(
        headers={**CODAL_HEADERS, **self._headers},
        verify=False,
        **common,
    )
    # Last-resort HTTP/1.1 + no-verify transport for TSETMC.
    self._fallback_client = httpx.AsyncClient(
        headers={**TSETMC_HEADERS, **self._headers},
        verify=False,
        **common,
    )

async def get(
    self,
    url: str,
    *,
    params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    raw: bool = False,
) -> httpx.Response:
    """Perform a GET request with retries and TLS fallbacks.

    The request is retried up to ``max_retries`` times on network errors,
    and responses with status codes >= 500 are treated as retryable.  A
    TSETMC connection that fails with ``SSLError``/``ConnectError`` is
    retried once over an insecure HTTP/1.1 transport.  Every ``*.codal.ir``
    request uses the dedicated certificate-relaxed transport.

    Args:
        url: Absolute request URL.
        params: Optional query parameters.  Ignored for URL encoding when
            ``raw`` is true.
        headers: Optional per-request headers merged over the defaults.
        raw: When true the URL string is sent verbatim without
            percent-encoding.  Required for the MarketWatch endpoint, whose
            ``paperTypes[0]=1`` brackets must stay literal.

    Returns:
        The successful :class:`httpx.Response`.

    Raises:
        NetworkError: If the host is unreachable, a non-2xx status is
            returned, or all retries are exhausted.

    Examples:
        >>> response = await client.get("https://cdn.tsetmc.com/api/BestLimits/1")
        >>> response.status_code
        200
    """

    target = self._build_url(url, params, raw=raw)

    try:
        async for attempt in self._retrying():
            with attempt:
                response = await self._send_with_fallback(target, headers)
                if response.status_code >= 500:
                    raise NetworkError(f"Server error {response.status_code} for {target}")
                response.raise_for_status()
                return response
    except httpx.HTTPStatusError as exc:
        raise NetworkError(f"HTTP {exc.response.status_code} for {exc.request.url}") from exc
    except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
        raise NetworkError(f"Request failed for {target}: {exc}") from exc

    raise NetworkError(f"Request failed after retries: {target}")

def int_to_date_optional(d_even: int | None) -> dt.date | None:
    """Convert a TSETMC ``dEven`` to a date, returning ``None`` for sentinels.

    Values such as ``0`` and ``1`` are emitted for inactive/expired instruments
    and placeholder rows.  Anything outside ``[19000101, 21001231]`` — or not a
    valid calendar date — yields ``None`` instead of raising.

    Args:
        d_even: An eight-digit Gregorian date encoded as an integer, or ``None``.

    Returns:
        The decoded :class:`datetime.date`, or ``None`` for sentinel or invalid
        values.

    Examples:
        >>> int_to_date_optional(20261028)
        datetime.date(2026, 10, 28)
        >>> int_to_date_optional(0) is None
        True
    """

    if d_even is None:
        return None
    try:
        value = int(d_even)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None
    if not MIN_EVEN_DATE <= value <= MAX_EVEN_DATE:
        return None
    try:
        return int_to_date(value)
    except ParseError:
        return None

    """Jalali counterpart of :func:`int_to_date_optional`.

    Args:
        d_even: An eight-digit Gregorian date encoded as an integer, or ``None``.

    Returns:
        The Jalali date as ``"YYYY-MM-DD"``, or ``None`` for sentinel values.

    Examples:
        >>> int_to_jdate_optional(1) is None
        True
    """

    gregorian = int_to_date_optional(d_even)
    if gregorian is None:
        return None
    jalali = jdatetime.date.fromgregorian(date=gregorian)
    return str(jalali.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"))

def normalize_persian(text: str) -> str:
    """Normalize Persian/Arabic text for reliable comparison.

    Converts Arabic yeh/kaf/teh-marbuta to their Persian equivalents, converts
    Arabic-Indic and Persian digits to ASCII digits, removes zero-width and
    directional control characters, and collapses whitespace.

    This is what makes ``"فولاد"`` written with an Arabic yeh and the same
    symbol written with a Persian yeh resolve to the same TSETMC instrument.

    Args:
        text: Any string, including Persian, Arabic-Indic or mixed text.

    Returns:
        The normalized string with single spaces and ASCII digits.

    Examples:
        >>> normalize_persian("۱۲۳")
        '123'
        >>> normalize_persian("  علي  ")
        'علی'
    """

    translated = text.translate(_CHAR_MAP).translate(_ZERO_WIDTH)
    return " ".join(translated.split())

async def search_symbol(
    client: AsyncHTTPClient,
    query: str,
) -> list[InstrumentSearchItem]:
    """Search TSETMC instruments by symbol or company name.

    The query is Persian-normalized before it is sent.  Results are memoized
    in-process by normalized query, so repeated searches do not hit the
    network.

    Args:
        client: An open :class:`~iranquant.core.client.AsyncHTTPClient`.
        query: Symbol or company-name fragment, e.g. ``"فولاد"`` or ``"خودرو"``.

    Returns:
        Matching instruments.  An empty query returns an empty list without a
        request.

    Raises:
        NetworkError: If ``cdn.tsetmc.com`` cannot be reached.
        ParseError: If the response does not match the expected schema.

    Examples:
        >>> items = await search_symbol(client, "فولاد")
        >>> items[0].lVal18AFC
        'فولاد'
    """

    normalized = normalize_persian(query)
    if not normalized:
        return []
    if normalized in _search_cache:
        return list(_search_cache[normalized])

    url = SYMBOL_SEARCH_URL.format(query=quote(normalized, safe=""))
    payload = await client.get_json(url)
    try:
        response = InstrumentSearchResponse.model_validate(payload)
    except Exception as exc:  # pydantic ValidationError
        raise ParseError(f"Unexpected instrument search payload for {query!r}") from exc

    items = response.instrumentSearch
    _search_cache[normalized] = items
    return list(items)

async def get_inscode(client: AsyncHTTPClient, symbol: str) -> str:
    """Resolve a symbol to its TSETMC instrument code (``insCode``).

    Matching is done on normalized ``lVal18AFC`` values.  Instruments with an
    active ``flow`` (1, 2 or 4) are preferred; ties are broken by the newest
    ``lastDate``.  Results are cached in-process.

    Args:
        client: An open :class:`~iranquant.core.client.AsyncHTTPClient`.
        symbol: Persian ticker, e.g. ``"فولاد"``.  Arabic yeh/kaf variants and
            Persian digits are normalized automatically.

    Returns:
        The numeric ``insCode`` as a string, e.g. ``"46348559193224090"``.

    Raises:
        SymbolNotFoundError: If the symbol is empty or no exact normalized
            match exists.
        NetworkError: If the search request fails.
        ParseError: If the search response is malformed.

    Examples:
        >>> code = await get_inscode(client, "فولاد")
        >>> code.isdigit()
        True
    """

    normalized = normalize_persian(symbol)
    if not normalized:
        raise SymbolNotFoundError("Empty symbol")

    cached = _inscode_cache.get(normalized)
    if cached is not None:
        return cached

    items = await search_symbol(client, normalized)
    matches = [item for item in items if normalize_persian(item.lVal18AFC) == normalized]
    if not matches:
        raise SymbolNotFoundError(f"Symbol not found: {symbol!r}")

    matches.sort(key=lambda item: (_is_active(item), item.lastDate or 0), reverse=True)
    code = matches[0].insCode
    _inscode_cache[normalized] = code
    return code

AsyncHTTPClient(
    *,
    timeout: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT,
    max_concurrency: int = MAX_CONCURRENCY,
    max_retries: int = MAX_RETRIES,
    retry_wait: float = RETRY_WAIT,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    proxy: str | None = None,
    trust_env: bool | None = None,
)

Small retrying wrapper around :class:httpx.AsyncClient.

Three transports are maintained:

  • a regular verified client used for TSETMC;
  • an insecure client used for every *.codal.ir domain, whose certificate chains frequently fail strict verification;
  • an insecure HTTP/1.1 fallback used once for TSETMC when the primary connection fails with an SSL/proxy-style error.

Environment proxy variables are ignored by default (trust_env=False) to avoid corporate/VPN HTTP proxies breaking direct connections to domestic Iranian hosts. Pass proxy=... to opt into an explicit proxy.

Create the pooled HTTP transports.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default timeout float

Per-request timeout in seconds. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT (30 s).

DEFAULT_TIMEOUT max_concurrency int

Maximum number of simultaneous requests enforced by an internal :class:asyncio.Semaphore. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.MAX_CONCURRENCY (10).

MAX_CONCURRENCY max_retries int

Total attempts per request. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.MAX_RETRIES (3).

MAX_RETRIES retry_wait float

Base wait used by the exponential retry backoff, in seconds. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.RETRY_WAIT (0.5).

RETRY_WAIT headers Mapping[str, str] | None

Extra headers merged over the built-in TSETMC/Codal headers.

None proxy str | None

Optional explicit proxy URL, e.g. "http://127.0.0.1:9090". When omitted, environment proxy variables are ignored.

None trust_env bool | None

Whether to honour HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY and other environment settings. Defaults to True only when an explicit proxy is supplied, otherwise False.

None

Examples:

>>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(timeout=10.0, max_concurrency=5)
>>> client.trust_env
False
>>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(proxy="http://127.0.0.1:9090")
>>> client.trust_env
True

def __init__(
    self,
    *,
    timeout: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT,
    max_concurrency: int = MAX_CONCURRENCY,
    max_retries: int = MAX_RETRIES,
    retry_wait: float = RETRY_WAIT,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    proxy: str | None = None,
    trust_env: bool | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Create the pooled HTTP transports.

    Args:
        timeout: Per-request timeout in seconds.  Defaults to
            :data:`iranquant.config.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT` (30 s).
        max_concurrency: Maximum number of simultaneous requests enforced
            by an internal :class:`asyncio.Semaphore`.  Defaults to
            :data:`iranquant.config.MAX_CONCURRENCY` (10).
        max_retries: Total attempts per request.  Defaults to
            :data:`iranquant.config.MAX_RETRIES` (3).
        retry_wait: Base wait used by the exponential retry backoff, in
            seconds.  Defaults to :data:`iranquant.config.RETRY_WAIT` (0.5).
        headers: Extra headers merged over the built-in TSETMC/Codal
            headers.
        proxy: Optional explicit proxy URL, e.g.
            ``"http://127.0.0.1:9090"``.  When omitted, environment proxy
            variables are ignored.
        trust_env: Whether to honour ``HTTP_PROXY`` / ``HTTPS_PROXY`` and
            other environment settings.  Defaults to ``True`` only when an
            explicit ``proxy`` is supplied, otherwise ``False``.

    Examples:
        >>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(timeout=10.0, max_concurrency=5)
        >>> client.trust_env
        False
        >>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(proxy="http://127.0.0.1:9090")
        >>> client.trust_env
        True
    """
    self._semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(max_concurrency)
    self._max_retries = max_retries
    self._retry_wait = retry_wait
    self._headers = dict(headers or {})
    self.proxy = proxy
    # Explicit proxies imply honouring the environment unless overridden.
    self.trust_env = (proxy is not None) if trust_env is None else trust_env

    common: dict[str, Any] = {
        "timeout": timeout,
        "follow_redirects": True,
        "trust_env": self.trust_env,
        "http2": False,
    }
    if proxy is not None:
        common["proxy"] = proxy

    self._client = httpx.AsyncClient(
        headers={**TSETMC_HEADERS, **self._headers},
        **common,
    )
    # Dedicated insecure transport for Codal (SSL chain bugs).
    self._codal_client = httpx.AsyncClient(
        headers={**CODAL_HEADERS, **self._headers},
        verify=False,
        **common,
    )
    # Last-resort HTTP/1.1 + no-verify transport for TSETMC.
    self._fallback_client = httpx.AsyncClient(
        headers={**TSETMC_HEADERS, **self._headers},
        verify=False,
        **common,
    )

async def get(
    self,
    url: str,
    *,
    params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    raw: bool = False,
) -> httpx.Response:
    """Perform a GET request with retries and TLS fallbacks.

    The request is retried up to ``max_retries`` times on network errors,
    and responses with status codes >= 500 are treated as retryable.  A
    TSETMC connection that fails with ``SSLError``/``ConnectError`` is
    retried once over an insecure HTTP/1.1 transport.  Every ``*.codal.ir``
    request uses the dedicated certificate-relaxed transport.

    Args:
        url: Absolute request URL.
        params: Optional query parameters.  Ignored for URL encoding when
            ``raw`` is true.
        headers: Optional per-request headers merged over the defaults.
        raw: When true the URL string is sent verbatim without
            percent-encoding.  Required for the MarketWatch endpoint, whose
            ``paperTypes[0]=1`` brackets must stay literal.

    Returns:
        The successful :class:`httpx.Response`.

    Raises:
        NetworkError: If the host is unreachable, a non-2xx status is
            returned, or all retries are exhausted.

    Examples:
        >>> response = await client.get("https://cdn.tsetmc.com/api/BestLimits/1")
        >>> response.status_code
        200
    """

    target = self._build_url(url, params, raw=raw)

    try:
        async for attempt in self._retrying():
            with attempt:
                response = await self._send_with_fallback(target, headers)
                if response.status_code >= 500:
                    raise NetworkError(f"Server error {response.status_code} for {target}")
                response.raise_for_status()
                return response
    except httpx.HTTPStatusError as exc:
        raise NetworkError(f"HTTP {exc.response.status_code} for {exc.request.url}") from exc
    except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
        raise NetworkError(f"Request failed for {target}: {exc}") from exc

    raise NetworkError(f"Request failed after retries: {target}")

def int_to_date(d_even: int) -> dt.date:
    """Convert a TSETMC ``dEven`` integer (e.g. ``20261028``) to a date.

    Args:
        d_even: An eight-digit Gregorian date encoded as an integer.

    Returns:
        The corresponding :class:`datetime.date`.

    Raises:
        ParseError: If the value is longer than eight digits or is not a valid
            calendar date.

    Examples:
        >>> int_to_date(20261028)
        datetime.date(2026, 10, 28)
    """

    raw = _even_digits(d_even, 8, "dEven")
    year, month, day = int(raw[:4]), int(raw[4:6]), int(raw[6:8])
    try:
        return dt.date(year, month, day)
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise ParseError(f"Invalid TSETMC date: {d_even!r}") from exc

def int_to_date_optional(d_even: int | None) -> dt.date | None:
    """Convert a TSETMC ``dEven`` to a date, returning ``None`` for sentinels.

    Values such as ``0`` and ``1`` are emitted for inactive/expired instruments
    and placeholder rows.  Anything outside ``[19000101, 21001231]`` — or not a
    valid calendar date — yields ``None`` instead of raising.

    Args:
        d_even: An eight-digit Gregorian date encoded as an integer, or ``None``.

    Returns:
        The decoded :class:`datetime.date`, or ``None`` for sentinel or invalid
        values.

    Examples:
        >>> int_to_date_optional(20261028)
        datetime.date(2026, 10, 28)
        >>> int_to_date_optional(0) is None
        True
    """

    if d_even is None:
        return None
    try:
        value = int(d_even)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None
    if not MIN_EVEN_DATE <= value <= MAX_EVEN_DATE:
        return None
    try:
        return int_to_date(value)
    except ParseError:
        return None

Backward-adjust prices using the priceYesterday gap ratio.

priceYesterday on day t already reflects any dividend or capital increase applied between t-1 and t, while final_price on day t-1 is unadjusted. The cumulative factor is therefore computed backwards from the newest day (factor 1.0) and applied to all price columns.

For i = n-2 ... 0 the per-day ratio is r[i] = prev_price[i+1] / final_price[i] and the cumulative factor is F[i] = F[i+1] * r[i]. Every column in PRICE_COLUMNS (open, high, low, close, final_price, prev_price) is multiplied by F[i]. The input list is never mutated.

fewer than two rows are returned as shallow copies.

Examples:

>>> rows = [
...     {"final_price": 100.0, "prev_price": 100.0, "open": 100.0,
...      "high": 100.0, "low": 100.0, "close": 100.0},
...     {"final_price": 100.0, "prev_price": 90.0, "open": 100.0,
...      "high": 100.0, "low": 100.0, "close": 100.0},

>>> apply_gap_adjustment(rows)[0]["final_price"]

def apply_gap_adjustment(records: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Backward-adjust prices using the ``priceYesterday`` gap ratio.

    ``priceYesterday`` on day *t* already reflects any dividend or capital
    increase applied between *t-1* and *t*, while ``final_price`` on day *t-1*
    is unadjusted.  The cumulative factor is therefore computed backwards from
    the newest day (factor 1.0) and applied to all price columns.

    For ``i = n-2 ... 0`` the per-day ratio is
    ``r[i] = prev_price[i+1] / final_price[i]`` and the cumulative factor is
    ``F[i] = F[i+1] * r[i]``.  Every column in ``PRICE_COLUMNS``
    (``open``, ``high``, ``low``, ``close``, ``final_price``, ``prev_price``)
    is multiplied by ``F[i]``.  The input list is never mutated.

    Args:
        records: Chronologically ascending daily records produced by
            :func:`_daily_records`.  Each record must contain the keys in
            ``PRICE_COLUMNS``.

    Returns:
        A new list of copied records with adjusted float prices.  Records with
        fewer than two rows are returned as shallow copies.

    Examples:
        >>> rows = [
        ...     {"final_price": 100.0, "prev_price": 100.0, "open": 100.0,
        ...      "high": 100.0, "low": 100.0, "close": 100.0},
        ...     {"final_price": 100.0, "prev_price": 90.0, "open": 100.0,
        ...      "high": 100.0, "low": 100.0, "close": 100.0},
        ... ]
        >>> apply_gap_adjustment(rows)[0]["final_price"]
        90.0
    """

    if len(records) < 2:
        return [dict(record) for record in records]

    factors = [1.0] * len(records)
    for index in range(len(records) - 2, -1, -1):
        previous_final = float(records[index]["final_price"])
        current_prev = float(records[index + 1]["prev_price"])
        ratio = current_prev / previous_final if previous_final > 0 and current_prev > 0 else 1.0
        factors[index] = factors[index + 1] * ratio

    adjusted: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for factor, record in zip(factors, records, strict=True):
        row = dict(record)
        for column in PRICE_COLUMNS:
            row[column] = float(record[column]) * factor
        adjusted.append(row)
    return adjusted

def apply_capital_adjustment(
    records: list[dict[str, Any]],
    share_changes: list[InstrumentShareChange],
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Adjust prices backwards for capital increases only.

    For an increase from ``numberOfShareOld`` to ``numberOfShareNew`` the
    historical prices preceding the event are multiplied by
    ``old / new`` (the theoretical ex-rights ratio).

    Events with non-positive share counts or an invalid ``dEven`` are ignored.
    A record exactly on the event date is *not* adjusted; only strictly earlier
    records are.  The input list is never mutated.

    Args:
        records: Chronologically ascending daily records with a
            ``datetime.date`` under the ``"date"`` key.
        share_changes: Corporate-action events from
            :func:`get_share_changes`.

    Returns:
        A new list of copied records whose ``PRICE_COLUMNS`` are scaled by the
        cumulative ``old / new`` factors of all later events.

    Examples:
        >>> event = InstrumentShareChange(
        ...     dEven=20261028, numberOfShareOld=100.0, numberOfShareNew=200.0
        ... )
        >>> apply_capital_adjustment(records, [event])[0]["open"]
        50.0
    """

    events: list[tuple[dt.date, InstrumentShareChange]] = []
    for event in share_changes:
        if event.numberOfShareOld <= 0 or event.numberOfShareNew <= 0:
            continue
        event_date = int_to_date_optional(event.dEven)
        if event_date is None:
            continue
        events.append((event_date, event))
    events.sort(key=lambda pair: pair[0])

    adjusted: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for record in records:
        row_date = cast(dt.date, record["date"])
        factor = 1.0
        for event_date, event in events:
            if row_date < event_date:
                factor *= event.numberOfShareOld / event.numberOfShareNew
        row = dict(record)
        for column in PRICE_COLUMNS:
            row[column] = float(record[column]) * factor
        adjusted.append(row)
    return adjusted

async def _daily_records(
    client: AsyncHTTPClient,
    ins_code: str,
    *,
    adjust: AdjustMode,
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    if adjust not in ("none", "all", "capital_only"):
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported adjust mode: {adjust!r}")

    payload = await client.get_json(DAILY_HISTORY_URL.format(ins_code=ins_code))
    response = cast(
        ClosingPriceDailyResponse,
        _validate(ClosingPriceDailyResponse, payload, "daily history"),
    )

    records: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for item in response.closingPriceDaily:
        # Drop sentinel dates emitted for expired/placeholder instruments.
        if item.dEven < MIN_EVEN_DATE:
            continue
        # Drop non-trading placeholder rows.
        if item.qTotTran5J == 0 and item.zTotTran == 0:
            continue
        records.append(
            {
                "date": int_to_date(item.dEven),
                "jdate": int_to_jdate(item.dEven),
                "open": item.priceFirst,
                "high": item.priceMax,
                "low": item.priceMin,
                "close": item.pDrCotVal,
                "final_price": item.pClosing,
                "prev_price": item.priceYesterday,
                "volume": item.qTotTran5J,
                "value": item.qTotCap,
                "trades": item.zTotTran,
            }
        )

    records.sort(key=lambda row: cast(dt.date, row["date"]))

    if adjust == "all":
        return apply_gap_adjustment(records)
    if adjust == "capital_only":
        changes = await get_share_changes(client, ins_code)
        return apply_capital_adjustment(records, changes)
    return records

    if not records:

    return to_dataframe(records, engine)

async def get_full_history(
    client: AsyncHTTPClient,
    ins_code: str,
    *,
    adjust: AdjustMode = "all",
    engine: Engine = "pandas",
) -> DataFrame:
    """Merge daily OHLCV with client-type history on the trading date.

    The two requests are performed sequentially and merged with an outer join
    on ``date`` (so dates missing from either source are retained), then sorted
    ascending.  The client-type ``jdate`` column is dropped, leaving a single
    ``jdate`` from the OHLCV frame.

    Args:
        client: An open :class:`~iranquant.core.client.AsyncHTTPClient`.
        ins_code: TSETMC instrument code.
        adjust: Price adjustment mode, identical to
            :func:`get_daily_history` (``"none"``, ``"all"`` or
            ``"capital_only"``).
        engine: ``"pandas"`` (default) or ``"polars"``.

    Returns:
        A frame with the eleven :func:`get_daily_history` columns followed by
        the twelve client-type columns below (``date`` is shared):

        * ``buy_I_Volume``, ``buy_N_Volume`` (``float``)
        * ``buy_I_Value``, ``buy_N_Value`` (``float``)
        * ``buy_N_Count``, ``buy_I_Count`` (``int``)
        * ``sell_I_Volume``, ``sell_N_Volume`` (``float``)
        * ``sell_I_Value``, ``sell_N_Value`` (``float``)
        * ``sell_N_Count``, ``sell_I_Count`` (``int``)

        When both sources are empty an empty frame is returned.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``adjust`` or ``engine`` is unsupported.
        NetworkError: If either request fails.
        ParseError: If either payload is malformed.

    Examples:
        >>> frame = await get_full_history(client, "46348559193224090")
        >>> {"open", "final_price", "buy_I_Volume"} <= set(frame.columns)
        True
    """

    daily = await _daily_records(client, ins_code, adjust=adjust)
    payload = await client.get_json(CLIENT_TYPE_HISTORY_URL.format(ins_code=ins_code))
    response = cast(
        ClientTypeResponse,
        _validate(ClientTypeResponse, payload, "client type history"),
    )
    clients = _client_type_records(response)

    daily_frame = pd.DataFrame(daily) if daily else pd.DataFrame(columns=HISTORY_COLUMNS)
    client_frame = pd.DataFrame(clients)
    if daily_frame.empty or client_frame.empty:
        merged = daily_frame
    else:
        client_frame = client_frame.drop(columns=["jdate"], errors="ignore")
        merged = daily_frame.merge(client_frame, on="date", how="outer")

    merged = merged.sort_values("date").reset_index(drop=True)

    if engine == "polars":
        return pl.from_pandas(merged)
    if engine == "pandas":
        return merged
    raise ValueError(f"Unsupported dataframe engine: {engine!r}")

AsyncHTTPClient(
    *,
    timeout: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT,
    max_concurrency: int = MAX_CONCURRENCY,
    max_retries: int = MAX_RETRIES,
    retry_wait: float = RETRY_WAIT,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    proxy: str | None = None,
    trust_env: bool | None = None,
)

Small retrying wrapper around :class:httpx.AsyncClient.

Three transports are maintained:

  • a regular verified client used for TSETMC;
  • an insecure client used for every *.codal.ir domain, whose certificate chains frequently fail strict verification;
  • an insecure HTTP/1.1 fallback used once for TSETMC when the primary connection fails with an SSL/proxy-style error.

Environment proxy variables are ignored by default (trust_env=False) to avoid corporate/VPN HTTP proxies breaking direct connections to domestic Iranian hosts. Pass proxy=... to opt into an explicit proxy.

Create the pooled HTTP transports.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default timeout float

Per-request timeout in seconds. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT (30 s).

DEFAULT_TIMEOUT max_concurrency int

Maximum number of simultaneous requests enforced by an internal :class:asyncio.Semaphore. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.MAX_CONCURRENCY (10).

MAX_CONCURRENCY max_retries int

Total attempts per request. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.MAX_RETRIES (3).

MAX_RETRIES retry_wait float

Base wait used by the exponential retry backoff, in seconds. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.RETRY_WAIT (0.5).

RETRY_WAIT headers Mapping[str, str] | None

Extra headers merged over the built-in TSETMC/Codal headers.

None proxy str | None

Optional explicit proxy URL, e.g. "http://127.0.0.1:9090". When omitted, environment proxy variables are ignored.

None trust_env bool | None

Whether to honour HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY and other environment settings. Defaults to True only when an explicit proxy is supplied, otherwise False.

None

Examples:

>>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(timeout=10.0, max_concurrency=5)
>>> client.trust_env
False
>>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(proxy="http://127.0.0.1:9090")
>>> client.trust_env
True

def __init__(
    self,
    *,
    timeout: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT,
    max_concurrency: int = MAX_CONCURRENCY,
    max_retries: int = MAX_RETRIES,
    retry_wait: float = RETRY_WAIT,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    proxy: str | None = None,
    trust_env: bool | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Create the pooled HTTP transports.

    Args:
        timeout: Per-request timeout in seconds.  Defaults to
            :data:`iranquant.config.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT` (30 s).
        max_concurrency: Maximum number of simultaneous requests enforced
            by an internal :class:`asyncio.Semaphore`.  Defaults to
            :data:`iranquant.config.MAX_CONCURRENCY` (10).
        max_retries: Total attempts per request.  Defaults to
            :data:`iranquant.config.MAX_RETRIES` (3).
        retry_wait: Base wait used by the exponential retry backoff, in
            seconds.  Defaults to :data:`iranquant.config.RETRY_WAIT` (0.5).
        headers: Extra headers merged over the built-in TSETMC/Codal
            headers.
        proxy: Optional explicit proxy URL, e.g.
            ``"http://127.0.0.1:9090"``.  When omitted, environment proxy
            variables are ignored.
        trust_env: Whether to honour ``HTTP_PROXY`` / ``HTTPS_PROXY`` and
            other environment settings.  Defaults to ``True`` only when an
            explicit ``proxy`` is supplied, otherwise ``False``.

    Examples:
        >>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(timeout=10.0, max_concurrency=5)
        >>> client.trust_env
        False
        >>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(proxy="http://127.0.0.1:9090")
        >>> client.trust_env
        True
    """
    self._semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(max_concurrency)
    self._max_retries = max_retries
    self._retry_wait = retry_wait
    self._headers = dict(headers or {})
    self.proxy = proxy
    # Explicit proxies imply honouring the environment unless overridden.
    self.trust_env = (proxy is not None) if trust_env is None else trust_env

    common: dict[str, Any] = {
        "timeout": timeout,
        "follow_redirects": True,
        "trust_env": self.trust_env,
        "http2": False,
    }
    if proxy is not None:
        common["proxy"] = proxy

    self._client = httpx.AsyncClient(
        headers={**TSETMC_HEADERS, **self._headers},
        **common,
    )
    # Dedicated insecure transport for Codal (SSL chain bugs).
    self._codal_client = httpx.AsyncClient(
        headers={**CODAL_HEADERS, **self._headers},
        verify=False,
        **common,
    )
    # Last-resort HTTP/1.1 + no-verify transport for TSETMC.
    self._fallback_client = httpx.AsyncClient(
        headers={**TSETMC_HEADERS, **self._headers},
        verify=False,
        **common,
    )

async def get(
    self,
    url: str,
    *,
    params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    raw: bool = False,
) -> httpx.Response:
    """Perform a GET request with retries and TLS fallbacks.

    The request is retried up to ``max_retries`` times on network errors,
    and responses with status codes >= 500 are treated as retryable.  A
    TSETMC connection that fails with ``SSLError``/``ConnectError`` is
    retried once over an insecure HTTP/1.1 transport.  Every ``*.codal.ir``
    request uses the dedicated certificate-relaxed transport.

    Args:
        url: Absolute request URL.
        params: Optional query parameters.  Ignored for URL encoding when
            ``raw`` is true.
        headers: Optional per-request headers merged over the defaults.
        raw: When true the URL string is sent verbatim without
            percent-encoding.  Required for the MarketWatch endpoint, whose
            ``paperTypes[0]=1`` brackets must stay literal.

    Returns:
        The successful :class:`httpx.Response`.

    Raises:
        NetworkError: If the host is unreachable, a non-2xx status is
            returned, or all retries are exhausted.

    Examples:
        >>> response = await client.get("https://cdn.tsetmc.com/api/BestLimits/1")
        >>> response.status_code
        200
    """

    target = self._build_url(url, params, raw=raw)

    try:
        async for attempt in self._retrying():
            with attempt:
                response = await self._send_with_fallback(target, headers)
                if response.status_code >= 500:
                    raise NetworkError(f"Server error {response.status_code} for {target}")
                response.raise_for_status()
                return response
    except httpx.HTTPStatusError as exc:
        raise NetworkError(f"HTTP {exc.response.status_code} for {exc.request.url}") from exc
    except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
        raise NetworkError(f"Request failed for {target}: {exc}") from exc

    raise NetworkError(f"Request failed after retries: {target}")

    self,
    url: str,
    *,
    params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    raw: bool = False,
) -> Any:

    response = await self.get(url, params=params, headers=headers, raw=raw)
    try:
        return response.json()
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise ParseError(f"Invalid JSON from {response.request.url}") from exc

def to_dataframe(records: list[dict[str, Any]], engine: Engine = "pandas") -> DataFrame:
    """Convert a list of record dictionaries to a Pandas or Polars DataFrame.

    An empty ``records`` list still produces a valid (empty) DataFrame for both
    engines.  Column order follows the key insertion order of the first record.

    Args:
        records: Row-oriented records, typically produced by the market and
            Codal modules.  Every record should share the same keys.
        engine: ``"pandas"`` (default) or ``"polars"``.

    Returns:
        A :class:`pandas.DataFrame` or :class:`polars.DataFrame` matching
        ``engine``.

    Raises:

           symbol   close
        0   فولاد  4150.0
        >>> to_dataframe([], engine="polars").height
        0
    """

    if engine == "polars":

    if engine == "pandas":

    raise ValueError(f"Unsupported dataframe engine: {engine!r}")

def int_to_time_optional(h_even: int | None) -> dt.time | None:
    """Convert a TSETMC ``hEven`` to a time, returning ``None`` when invalid.

    Args:
        h_even: A ``HHMMSS`` time encoded as an integer, or ``None``.

    Returns:
        The decoded :class:`datetime.time`, or ``None`` when the value is not a
        valid time between ``00:00:00`` and ``23:59:59``.

    Examples:
        >>> int_to_time_optional(91500)
        datetime.time(9, 15)
        >>> int_to_time_optional(999999) is None
        True
    """

    if h_even is None:
        return None
    try:
        value = int(h_even)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None
    if not 0 <= value <= 235959:
        return None
    try:
        return int_to_time(value)
    except ParseError:
        return None

Converts Arabic yeh/kaf/teh-marbuta to their Persian equivalents, converts Arabic-Indic and Persian digits to ASCII digits, removes zero-width and directional control characters, and collapses whitespace.

def normalize_persian(text: str) -> str:
    """Normalize Persian/Arabic text for reliable comparison.

    Converts Arabic yeh/kaf/teh-marbuta to their Persian equivalents, converts
    Arabic-Indic and Persian digits to ASCII digits, removes zero-width and
    directional control characters, and collapses whitespace.

    This is what makes ``"فولاد"`` written with an Arabic yeh and the same
    symbol written with a Persian yeh resolve to the same TSETMC instrument.

    Args:
        text: Any string, including Persian, Arabic-Indic or mixed text.

    Returns:
        The normalized string with single spaces and ASCII digits.

    Examples:
        >>> normalize_persian("۱۲۳")
        '123'
        >>> normalize_persian("  علي  ")
        'علی'
    """

    translated = text.translate(_CHAR_MAP).translate(_ZERO_WIDTH)
    return " ".join(translated.split())

def _first_value(*values: float | None) -> float:

async def get_market_watch(
    client: AsyncHTTPClient,
    *,
    engine: Engine = "pandas",
) -> DataFrame:
    """Fetch the entire market snapshot in a single request.

    The request is sent verbatim (``raw=True``) so the bracketed
    ``paperTypes[0]=1`` query is never percent-encoded.

    Args:
        client: An open :class:`~iranquant.core.client.AsyncHTTPClient`.
        engine: ``"pandas"`` (default) or ``"polars"``.

    Returns:
        One row per symbol with the following columns:

        =================  ==========================  =======================
        Column             Type                        Description
        =================  ==========================  =======================
        ``ins_code``       ``str``                     TSETMC instrument code.
        ``symbol``         ``str``                     Ticker (``lva``).
        ``company_name``   ``str``                     Company name (``lvc``).
        ``eps``            ``float | None``            Earnings per share.
        ``pe``             ``float | None``            Price-to-earnings ratio.
        ``open``           ``float``                   Opening price (``pf``).
        ``high``           ``float``                   Daily high (``pmx``).
        ``low``            ``float``                   Daily low (``pmn``).
        ``close``          ``float``                   Last trade (``pdv``).
        ``final_price``    ``float``                   Closing price (``pcl``).
        ``prev_price``     ``float``                   Previous close (``py``).
        ``volume``         ``float``                   Volume (``qtj``/``qtt``).
        ``value``          ``float``                   Value in Rials (``qtc``).
        ``trades``         ``float``                   Trade count (``ztt``).
        ``tmax``           ``float``                   High limit (``pMax``/``ps``).
        ``tmin``           ``float``                   Low limit (``pMin``/``pi``).
        ``total_shares``   ``float``                   Listed shares (``ztd``).
        ``order_book``     ``list[dict[str, float]]``  Best-limit levels.
        =================  ==========================  =======================

        ``order_book`` dictionaries expose ``n``, ``qmd``, ``zmd``, ``pmd``,
        ``pmo``, ``zmo`` and ``qmo`` for levels 1..5, sorted by ``n``.

    Raises:
        NetworkError: If the MarketWatch endpoint cannot be reached.
        ParseError: If the response body is not valid JSON.
        pydantic.ValidationError: If the payload does not match the schema.

    Examples:
        >>> market = await get_market_watch(client)
        >>> market[["symbol", "close", "tmax"]].head()
        >>> book = market.iloc[0]["order_book"]
        >>> book[0]["zmd"]  # best bid volume
    """

    payload = await client.get_json(MARKET_WATCH_URL, raw=True)
    response = MarketWatchResponse.model_validate(payload)

    records: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for item in response.marketwatch:
        order_book = sorted(item.blDs, key=lambda level: level.n)
        records.append(
            {
                "ins_code": item.insCode,
                "symbol": normalize_persian(item.lva),
                "company_name": normalize_persian(item.lvc),
                "eps": item.eps,
                "pe": item.pe,
                "open": item.pf,
                "high": item.pmx,
                "low": item.pmn,
                "close": item.pdv,
                "final_price": item.pcl,
                "prev_price": item.py,
                # Current servers use qtj/pMax/pMin; fall back to legacy names.
                "volume": _first_value(item.qtj, item.qtt),
                "value": item.qtc,
                "trades": item.ztt,
                "tmax": _first_value(item.pMax, item.ps),
                "tmin": _first_value(item.pMin, item.pi),
                "total_shares": item.ztd,
                "order_book": [level.model_dump() for level in order_book],
            }
        )
    return to_dataframe(records, engine)

async def get_order_book(
    client: AsyncHTTPClient,
    ins_code: str,
    *,
    engine: Engine = "pandas",
) -> DataFrame:
    """Fetch the best-limit order book (levels 1..5) for an instrument.

    Rows are sorted by level number.  The ``d``/``o`` suffixes mean *demand*
    (buy) and *offer* (sell) respectively.

    Args:
        client: An open :class:`~iranquant.core.client.AsyncHTTPClient`.
        ins_code: TSETMC instrument code.
        engine: ``"pandas"`` (default) or ``"polars"``.

    Returns:
        A frame with one row per visible level and these columns:

        * ``n`` (``int``) — level number (1 is the best level).
        * ``qmd`` (``float``) — bid order count.
        * ``zmd`` (``float``) — bid volume.
        * ``pmd`` (``float``) — bid price.
        * ``pmo`` (``float``) — ask price.
        * ``zmo`` (``float``) — ask volume.
        * ``qmo`` (``float``) — ask order count.

    Raises:
        NetworkError: If the endpoint cannot be reached.
        ParseError: If the response body is not valid JSON.
        pydantic.ValidationError: If the payload does not match the schema.

    Examples:
        >>> book = await get_order_book(client, "46348559193224090")
        >>> book.iloc[0][["pmd", "zmd", "pmo", "zmo"]]
    """

    payload = await client.get_json(BEST_LIMITS_URL.format(ins_code=ins_code))
    response = BestLimitResponse.model_validate(payload)

    records = [
        {
            "n": level.number,
            "qmd": level.qTitMeDem,
            "zmd": level.zOrdMeDem,
            "pmd": level.pMeDem,
            "pmo": level.pMeOf,
            "zmo": level.zOrdMeOf,
            "qmo": level.qTitMeOf,
        }
        for level in sorted(response.bestLimits, key=lambda level: level.number)
    ]
    return to_dataframe(records, engine)

AsyncHTTPClient(
    *,
    timeout: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT,
    max_concurrency: int = MAX_CONCURRENCY,
    max_retries: int = MAX_RETRIES,
    retry_wait: float = RETRY_WAIT,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    proxy: str | None = None,
    trust_env: bool | None = None,
)

Small retrying wrapper around :class:httpx.AsyncClient.

Three transports are maintained:

  • a regular verified client used for TSETMC;
  • an insecure client used for every *.codal.ir domain, whose certificate chains frequently fail strict verification;
  • an insecure HTTP/1.1 fallback used once for TSETMC when the primary connection fails with an SSL/proxy-style error.

Environment proxy variables are ignored by default (trust_env=False) to avoid corporate/VPN HTTP proxies breaking direct connections to domestic Iranian hosts. Pass proxy=... to opt into an explicit proxy.

Create the pooled HTTP transports.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default timeout float

Per-request timeout in seconds. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT (30 s).

DEFAULT_TIMEOUT max_concurrency int

Maximum number of simultaneous requests enforced by an internal :class:asyncio.Semaphore. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.MAX_CONCURRENCY (10).

MAX_CONCURRENCY max_retries int

Total attempts per request. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.MAX_RETRIES (3).

MAX_RETRIES retry_wait float

Base wait used by the exponential retry backoff, in seconds. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.RETRY_WAIT (0.5).

RETRY_WAIT headers Mapping[str, str] | None

Extra headers merged over the built-in TSETMC/Codal headers.

None proxy str | None

Optional explicit proxy URL, e.g. "http://127.0.0.1:9090". When omitted, environment proxy variables are ignored.

None trust_env bool | None

Whether to honour HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY and other environment settings. Defaults to True only when an explicit proxy is supplied, otherwise False.

None

Examples:

>>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(timeout=10.0, max_concurrency=5)
>>> client.trust_env
False
>>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(proxy="http://127.0.0.1:9090")
>>> client.trust_env
True

def __init__(
    self,
    *,
    timeout: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT,
    max_concurrency: int = MAX_CONCURRENCY,
    max_retries: int = MAX_RETRIES,
    retry_wait: float = RETRY_WAIT,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    proxy: str | None = None,
    trust_env: bool | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Create the pooled HTTP transports.

    Args:
        timeout: Per-request timeout in seconds.  Defaults to
            :data:`iranquant.config.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT` (30 s).
        max_concurrency: Maximum number of simultaneous requests enforced
            by an internal :class:`asyncio.Semaphore`.  Defaults to
            :data:`iranquant.config.MAX_CONCURRENCY` (10).
        max_retries: Total attempts per request.  Defaults to
            :data:`iranquant.config.MAX_RETRIES` (3).
        retry_wait: Base wait used by the exponential retry backoff, in
            seconds.  Defaults to :data:`iranquant.config.RETRY_WAIT` (0.5).
        headers: Extra headers merged over the built-in TSETMC/Codal
            headers.
        proxy: Optional explicit proxy URL, e.g.
            ``"http://127.0.0.1:9090"``.  When omitted, environment proxy
            variables are ignored.
        trust_env: Whether to honour ``HTTP_PROXY`` / ``HTTPS_PROXY`` and
            other environment settings.  Defaults to ``True`` only when an
            explicit ``proxy`` is supplied, otherwise ``False``.

    Examples:
        >>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(timeout=10.0, max_concurrency=5)
        >>> client.trust_env
        False
        >>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(proxy="http://127.0.0.1:9090")
        >>> client.trust_env
        True
    """
    self._semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(max_concurrency)
    self._max_retries = max_retries
    self._retry_wait = retry_wait
    self._headers = dict(headers or {})
    self.proxy = proxy
    # Explicit proxies imply honouring the environment unless overridden.
    self.trust_env = (proxy is not None) if trust_env is None else trust_env

    common: dict[str, Any] = {
        "timeout": timeout,
        "follow_redirects": True,
        "trust_env": self.trust_env,
        "http2": False,
    }
    if proxy is not None:
        common["proxy"] = proxy

    self._client = httpx.AsyncClient(
        headers={**TSETMC_HEADERS, **self._headers},
        **common,
    )
    # Dedicated insecure transport for Codal (SSL chain bugs).
    self._codal_client = httpx.AsyncClient(
        headers={**CODAL_HEADERS, **self._headers},
        verify=False,
        **common,
    )
    # Last-resort HTTP/1.1 + no-verify transport for TSETMC.
    self._fallback_client = httpx.AsyncClient(
        headers={**TSETMC_HEADERS, **self._headers},
        verify=False,
        **common,
    )

async def get(
    self,
    url: str,
    *,
    params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    raw: bool = False,
) -> httpx.Response:
    """Perform a GET request with retries and TLS fallbacks.

    The request is retried up to ``max_retries`` times on network errors,
    and responses with status codes >= 500 are treated as retryable.  A
    TSETMC connection that fails with ``SSLError``/``ConnectError`` is
    retried once over an insecure HTTP/1.1 transport.  Every ``*.codal.ir``
    request uses the dedicated certificate-relaxed transport.

    Args:
        url: Absolute request URL.
        params: Optional query parameters.  Ignored for URL encoding when
            ``raw`` is true.
        headers: Optional per-request headers merged over the defaults.
        raw: When true the URL string is sent verbatim without
            percent-encoding.  Required for the MarketWatch endpoint, whose
            ``paperTypes[0]=1`` brackets must stay literal.

    Returns:
        The successful :class:`httpx.Response`.

    Raises:
        NetworkError: If the host is unreachable, a non-2xx status is
            returned, or all retries are exhausted.

    Examples:
        >>> response = await client.get("https://cdn.tsetmc.com/api/BestLimits/1")
        >>> response.status_code
        200
    """

    target = self._build_url(url, params, raw=raw)

    try:
        async for attempt in self._retrying():
            with attempt:
                response = await self._send_with_fallback(target, headers)
                if response.status_code >= 500:
                    raise NetworkError(f"Server error {response.status_code} for {target}")
                response.raise_for_status()
                return response
    except httpx.HTTPStatusError as exc:
        raise NetworkError(f"HTTP {exc.response.status_code} for {exc.request.url}") from exc
    except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
        raise NetworkError(f"Request failed for {target}: {exc}") from exc

    raise NetworkError(f"Request failed after retries: {target}")

def int_to_date_optional(d_even: int | None) -> dt.date | None:
    """Convert a TSETMC ``dEven`` to a date, returning ``None`` for sentinels.

    Values such as ``0`` and ``1`` are emitted for inactive/expired instruments
    and placeholder rows.  Anything outside ``[19000101, 21001231]`` — or not a
    valid calendar date — yields ``None`` instead of raising.

    Args:
        d_even: An eight-digit Gregorian date encoded as an integer, or ``None``.

    Returns:
        The decoded :class:`datetime.date`, or ``None`` for sentinel or invalid
        values.

    Examples:
        >>> int_to_date_optional(20261028)
        datetime.date(2026, 10, 28)
        >>> int_to_date_optional(0) is None
        True
    """

    if d_even is None:
        return None
    try:
        value = int(d_even)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None
    if not MIN_EVEN_DATE <= value <= MAX_EVEN_DATE:
        return None
    try:
        return int_to_date(value)
    except ParseError:
        return None

normalize_persian(text: str) -> str

Normalize Persian/Arabic text for reliable comparison.

Converts Arabic yeh/kaf/teh-marbuta to their Persian equivalents, converts Arabic-Indic and Persian digits to ASCII digits, removes zero-width and directional control characters, and collapses whitespace.

This is what makes "فولاد" written with an Arabic yeh and the same symbol written with a Persian yeh resolve to the same TSETMC instrument.

Parameters:
