async def fetch_and_parse_report(
    url_or_letter: str | CodalLetter,
    engine: Engine = "pandas",
    *,
    client: AsyncHTTPClient | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Download a Codal report page and parse all of its datasource tables.

    Relative URLs (including those on :class:`~iranquant.models.codal.CodalLetter`)
    are resolved with :func:`~iranquant.codal.search.resolve_codal_url` before
    the request is made.

    Args:
        url_or_letter: Either an absolute/relative report URL or a
            ``CodalLetter`` whose ``Url`` is used.
        engine: ``"pandas"`` (default) or ``"polars"``.
        client: Optional shared :class:`~iranquant.core.client.AsyncHTTPClient`.
            When omitted a temporary client is used and closed.

    Returns:
        The dictionary produced by :func:`parse_codal_tables`, keyed by
        ``"<sheet title> - <table title>"``.

    Raises:
        NetworkError: If the report page cannot be downloaded.
        ParseError: If the page has no valid ``var datasource`` JSON or the
            datasource structure is invalid.
        ValueError: If ``engine`` is unsupported.

    Examples:
        >>> letter = reports.Letters[0]
        >>> tables = await fetch_and_parse_report(letter)
        >>> for name, table in tables.items():
        ...     print(name, table.shape)
    """

    url = url_or_letter.Url if isinstance(url_or_letter, CodalLetter) else url_or_letter
    url = resolve_codal_url(url)

    if client is not None:
        return await _fetch_and_parse(client, url, engine)

    http = AsyncHTTPClient()
    try:
        return await _fetch_and_parse(http, url, engine)
    finally:
        await http.aclose()

async def search_codal(
    symbol: str | None = None,
    letter_type: int = -1,
    category: int = -1,
    page: int = 1,
    audited: bool = True,
    not_audited: bool = True,
    mains: bool = True,
    childs: bool = True,
    *,
    client: AsyncHTTPClient | None = None,
) -> CodalSearchResponse:
    """Search Codal announcements.

    Parameters mirror the ``search.codal.ir`` query API.  A temporary client is
    created and closed when ``client`` is not supplied.  Every returned letter
    has its ``Url``, ``ExcelUrl`` and ``PdfUrl`` resolved to absolute URLs.

    Args:
        symbol: Optional Persian ticker to filter by, e.g. ``"فولاد"``.
        letter_type: Codal ``LetterType`` filter.  ``-1`` means all types;
            ``58`` selects monthly activity reports and ``6`` selects interim
            financial statements.  Defaults to ``-1``.
        category: Codal ``Category`` filter; ``-1`` means all.  Defaults to
            ``-1``.
        page: One-based result page.  Defaults to ``1``.
        audited: Include audited reports.  Defaults to ``True``.
        not_audited: Include unaudited reports.  Defaults to ``True``.
        mains: Include parent-company reports.  Defaults to ``True``.
        childs: Include subsidiary reports.  Defaults to ``True``.
        client: Optional shared :class:`~iranquant.core.client.AsyncHTTPClient`.
            When omitted a temporary client is used and closed.

    Returns:
        A :class:`~iranquant.models.codal.CodalSearchResponse` with ``Total``,
        ``Page`` and a list of :class:`~iranquant.models.codal.CodalLetter`.

    Raises:
        NetworkError: If ``search.codal.ir`` cannot be reached.
        ParseError: If the response is not valid JSON or does not match the
            expected schema.

    Examples:
        >>> response = await search_codal("فولاد", letter_type=58)
        >>> response.Total
        12
        >>> response.Letters[0].Url.startswith("https://codal.ir")
        True
    """

    if client is not None:
        return await _search(
            client,
            symbol=symbol,
            letter_type=letter_type,
            category=category,
            page=page,
            audited=audited,
            not_audited=not_audited,
            mains=mains,
            childs=childs,
        )

    http = AsyncHTTPClient()
    try:
        return await _search(
            http,
            symbol=symbol,
            letter_type=letter_type,
            category=category,
            page=page,
            audited=audited,
            not_audited=not_audited,
            mains=mains,
            childs=childs,
        )
    finally:
        await http.aclose()

async def monthly_sales_summary(
    symbol: str,
    page: int = 1,
    *,
    client: AsyncHTTPClient | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Fetch and analyze a symbol's latest monthly sales report.

    The newest report on ``page`` is parsed, and its previous distinct monthly
    period is parsed too so a true Month-over-Month comparison can be computed.

    Args:
        symbol: Persian ticker, e.g. ``"فولاد"``.
        page: One-based Codal result page.  Defaults to ``1``.
        client: Optional shared :class:`~iranquant.core.client.AsyncHTTPClient`.

    Returns:
        The dictionary from :func:`analyze_monthly_sales` plus
        ``symbol``, ``tracing_no``, ``title``, ``prev_month_tracing_no`` and a
        ``mom_change_pct`` derived from the previous month's report.

    Raises:
        ParseError: If Codal returns no HTML monthly reports.
        NetworkError: If Codal or the report page cannot be fetched.
        ValueError: If the latest report has no usable tables.

    Examples:
        >>> summary = await monthly_sales_summary("فولاد")
        >>> summary["current_month_sales"]
        >>> summary["mom_change_pct"]
    """

    reports = await get_monthly_reports(symbol, page=page, client=client)
    letters = [letter for letter in reports.Letters if letter.HasHtml and letter.Url]
    if not letters:
        raise ParseError(f"No HTML monthly report found for {symbol!r}")

    def sort_key(letter: Any) -> tuple[tuple[int, int, int], int]:
        period = _letter_period(letter) or (0, 0, 0)
        return period, int(getattr(letter, "TracingNo", 0) or 0)

    ordered = sorted(letters, key=sort_key, reverse=True)
    latest = ordered[0]
    latest_period = _letter_period(latest)

    tables = await fetch_and_parse_report(latest, client=client)
    result = analyze_monthly_sales(tables)
    result.update(
        {
            "symbol": normalize_persian(symbol),
            "tracing_no": latest.TracingNo,
            "title": latest.Title,
            "page": page,
        }
    )

    previous = next(
        (
            letter
            for letter in ordered[1:]
            if latest_period is None or (_letter_period(letter) or (0, 0, 0)) < latest_period
        ),
        None,
    )
    if previous is None:
        return result

    try:
        previous_tables = await fetch_and_parse_report(previous, client=client)
        previous_result = analyze_monthly_sales(previous_tables)
    except (IranQuantError, ValueError, TypeError):
        return result

    previous_sales = previous_result.get("current_month_sales")
    if isinstance(previous_sales, (int, float)):
        result["prev_month_sales"] = float(previous_sales)
        result["prev_month_tracing_no"] = previous.TracingNo
        current_sales = result.get("current_month_sales")
        result["mom_change_pct"] = _pct_change(
            float(current_sales) if isinstance(current_sales, (int, float)) else None,
            float(previous_sales),
        )
    return result

def to_dataframe(records: list[dict[str, Any]], engine: Engine = "pandas") -> DataFrame:
    """Convert a list of record dictionaries to a Pandas or Polars DataFrame.

    An empty ``records`` list still produces a valid (empty) DataFrame for both
    engines.  Column order follows the key insertion order of the first record.

    Args:
        records: Row-oriented records, typically produced by the market and
            Codal modules.  Every record should share the same keys.
        engine: ``"pandas"`` (default) or ``"polars"``.

    Returns:
        A :class:`pandas.DataFrame` or :class:`polars.DataFrame` matching
        ``engine``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``engine`` is neither ``"pandas"`` nor ``"polars"``.

    Examples:
        >>> to_dataframe([{"symbol": "فولاد", "close": 4150.0}])
           symbol   close
        0   فولاد  4150.0
        >>> to_dataframe([], engine="polars").height
        0
    """

    if engine == "polars":
        return pl.DataFrame(records)
    if engine == "pandas":
        return cast(pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame(records))
    raise ValueError(f"Unsupported dataframe engine: {engine!r}")

def normalize_persian(text: str) -> str:
    """Normalize Persian/Arabic text for reliable comparison.

    Converts Arabic yeh/kaf/teh-marbuta to their Persian equivalents, converts
    Arabic-Indic and Persian digits to ASCII digits, removes zero-width and
    directional control characters, and collapses whitespace.

    This is what makes ``"فولاد"`` written with an Arabic yeh and the same
    symbol written with a Persian yeh resolve to the same TSETMC instrument.

    Args:
        text: Any string, including Persian, Arabic-Indic or mixed text.

    Returns:
        The normalized string with single spaces and ASCII digits.

    Examples:
        >>> normalize_persian("۱۲۳")
        '123'
        >>> normalize_persian("  علي  ")
        'علی'
    """

    translated = text.translate(_CHAR_MAP).translate(_ZERO_WIDTH)
    return " ".join(translated.split())

def run_sync(coro: Coroutine[Any, Any, T]) -> T:
    """Run ``coro`` to completion from synchronous code.

    A plain ``asyncio.run`` is used when no event loop is running.  Inside an
    already-running loop (Jupyter, Colab, async applications) the coroutine is
    executed on a fresh loop in a background thread, which avoids the usual
    "asyncio.run() cannot be called from a running event loop" error.

    Args:
        coro: An already-created coroutine object.

    Returns:
        Whatever the coroutine returns.

    Raises:
        BaseException: Any exception raised by the coroutine is re-raised in
            the calling thread.

    Examples:
        >>> async def answer() -> int:
        ...     return 42
        >>> run_sync(answer())
        42
    """

    try:
        asyncio.get_running_loop()
    except RuntimeError:
        return asyncio.run(coro)
    return _run_in_thread(coro)

def compute_money_flow(frame: DataFrame, vol_window: int = 20) -> DataFrame:
    """Add smart-money, per-capita and real/legal flow columns.

    Works with both Pandas and Polars inputs and returns a frame of the same
    type.  All monetary per-capita values are expressed in Rials
    (``*_m`` variants are in million Tomans).

    The required input columns are ``final_price``, ``close``, ``volume``,
    ``buy_I_Volume``, ``sell_I_Volume``, ``buy_I_Count`` and ``sell_I_Count``
    (all present in :func:`iranquant.full_history`).  Columns are computed as:

    * ``real_buy_per_capita = buy_I_Volume * final_price / max(buy_I_Count, 1)``
    * ``real_sell_per_capita = sell_I_Volume * final_price / max(sell_I_Count, 1)``
    * ``buyer_power_ratio = real_buy_per_capita / max(real_sell_per_capita, 1)``
    * ``net_real_value = (buy_I_Volume - sell_I_Volume) * final_price``
    * ``ownership_change_pct = ((buy_I_Volume - sell_I_Volume) / max(volume, 1)) * 100``
    * ``close_vs_final_pct = ((close - final_price) / max(final_price, 1)) * 100``
    * ``vol_ratio = volume / rolling_mean(volume, vol_window)``

    ``smart_money_entry`` is ``True`` when ``vol_ratio >= 1.8`` **and**
    ``buyer_power_ratio >= 1.5`` **and** ``net_real_value > 0`` **and**
    ``close >= final_price``.  ``smart_money_exit`` mirrors it with
    ``buyer_power_ratio <= 0.67``, ``net_real_value < 0`` and
    ``close <= final_price``.

    Args:
        frame: A history frame.  Any extra columns (including ``date`` and
            ``jdate``) are preserved unchanged.
        vol_window: Rolling window used for the volume-ratio baseline.  Must be
            at least ``1``.  Defaults to ``20``.

    Returns:
        A frame of the same engine with all input columns plus:

        * ``real_buy_per_capita`` (``float``) — Rials per retail buy order.
        * ``real_buy_per_capita_m`` (``float``) — same, in million Tomans.
        * ``real_sell_per_capita`` (``float``) — Rials per retail sell order.
        * ``real_sell_per_capita_m`` (``float``) — same, in million Tomans.
        * ``buyer_power_ratio`` (``float``) — real buy/sell power ratio.
        * ``net_real_value`` (``float``) — net real money flow in Rials.
        * ``ownership_change_pct`` (``float``) — net real volume / total volume.
        * ``close_vs_final_pct`` (``float``) — last price vs closing price.
        * ``vol_ratio`` (``float``) — volume relative to its rolling mean.
        * ``smart_money_entry`` (``bool``) — smart-money accumulation signal.
        * ``smart_money_exit`` (``bool``) — smart-money distribution signal.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``vol_window < 1``.
        KeyError: If any required input column is missing.

    Examples:
        >>> flow = compute_money_flow(iq.full_history("فولاد"))
        >>> flow[["jdate", "buyer_power_ratio", "smart_money_entry"]].tail(3)

        The Polars path preserves ``pl.DataFrame``::

        >>> import polars as pl
        >>> flow = compute_money_flow(iq.full_history("فولاد", engine="polars"))
        >>> flow.filter(pl.col("smart_money_entry")).height
    """

    if vol_window < 1:
        raise ValueError("vol_window must be >= 1")

    source = to_pandas(frame)
    missing = [column for column in _REQUIRED if column not in source.columns]
    if missing:
        raise KeyError(f"Missing required columns: {', '.join(missing)}")

    out = source.copy()
    final_price = cast(pd.Series, out["final_price"].astype(float))
    close = cast(pd.Series, out["close"].astype(float))
    volume = cast(pd.Series, out["volume"].astype(float))
    buy_i_volume = cast(pd.Series, out["buy_I_Volume"].astype(float))
    sell_i_volume = cast(pd.Series, out["sell_I_Volume"].astype(float))
    buy_i_count = cast(pd.Series, out["buy_I_Count"].astype(float))
    sell_i_count = cast(pd.Series, out["sell_I_Count"].astype(float))

    real_buy = (buy_i_volume * final_price) / buy_i_count.clip(lower=1.0)
    real_sell = (sell_i_volume * final_price) / sell_i_count.clip(lower=1.0)
    buyer_power = real_buy / real_sell.clip(lower=1.0)

    net_real_value = (buy_i_volume - sell_i_volume) * final_price
    ownership_change = ((buy_i_volume - sell_i_volume) / volume.clip(lower=1.0)) * 100.0
    close_vs_final = ((close - final_price) / final_price.clip(lower=1.0)) * 100.0

    rolling_volume = volume.rolling(vol_window, min_periods=1).mean()
    vol_ratio = (volume / rolling_volume.clip(lower=1e-9)).fillna(0.0)

    out["real_buy_per_capita"] = real_buy
    out["real_buy_per_capita_m"] = real_buy / 1e7
    out["real_sell_per_capita"] = real_sell
    out["real_sell_per_capita_m"] = real_sell / 1e7
    out["buyer_power_ratio"] = buyer_power
    out["net_real_value"] = net_real_value
    out["ownership_change_pct"] = ownership_change
    out["close_vs_final_pct"] = close_vs_final
    out["vol_ratio"] = vol_ratio
    out["smart_money_entry"] = (
        (vol_ratio >= 1.8) & (buyer_power >= 1.5) & (net_real_value > 0) & (close >= final_price)
    )
    out["smart_money_exit"] = (
        (vol_ratio >= 1.8) & (buyer_power <= 0.67) & (net_real_value < 0) & (close <= final_price)
    )
    return restore(frame, out)

Compute a signed multi-timeframe Kaufman efficiency power score.

For each window w the signed Kaufman efficiency ratio is::

def compute_movement_power(
    frame: DataFrame,
    windows: tuple[int, int, int] = (5, 20, 60),
) -> DataFrame:
    """Compute a signed multi-timeframe Kaufman efficiency power score.

    For each window ``w`` the signed Kaufman efficiency ratio is::

        er_w = sign(close - close.shift(w))
               * abs(close - close.shift(w))
               / rolling_sum(abs(close.diff()), w)

    The score starts as a weighted sum of the signed ratios.  With exactly
    three windows the weights are ``(0.5, 0.3, 0.2)``; otherwise all windows
    are equally weighted.  The score is then multiplied by a volume factor
    (``volume / rolling_mean(volume, min(windows))`` clipped to ``[0.5, 2.0]``)
    and, when present, a buyer-power factor
    (``clip(buyer_power_ratio, 0.5, 3.0) / 1.5`` clipped to ``[0.5, 1.5]``),
    scaled by ``100`` and clipped to ``[-100, +100]``.

    Args:
        frame: A history frame containing ``close``.  ``volume`` and
            ``buyer_power_ratio`` (produced by :func:`compute_money_flow`) are
            optional and only modulate the score when present.
        windows: One or more positive lookback windows.  Defaults to
            ``(5, 20, 60)``.

    Returns:
        A frame of the same engine with all input columns plus:

        * ``er_<window>`` (``float``) — signed efficiency ratio per window
        (for example ``er_5``, ``er_20``, ``er_60``).
        * ``movement_power_score`` (``float``) — weighted, volume- and
        buyer-power-adjusted score in ``[-100, +100]``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``windows`` is empty or contains a non-positive value.
        KeyError: If the ``close`` column is missing.

    Examples:
        >>> power = compute_movement_power(iq.full_history("فولاد"))
        >>> power[["jdate", "er_5", "er_20", "movement_power_score"]].tail(3)
        >>> power.sort_values("movement_power_score", ascending=False).head()
    """

    if not windows:
        raise ValueError("At least one window is required")
    if any(window < 1 for window in windows):
        raise ValueError("Windows must be positive integers")

    source = to_pandas(frame)
    if "close" not in source.columns:
        raise KeyError("Missing required column: close")
    if source.empty:
        out = source.copy()
        for window in windows:
            out[f"er_{window}"] = pd.Series(dtype=float)
        out["movement_power_score"] = pd.Series(dtype=float)
        return restore(frame, out)

    out = source.copy()
    close = cast(pd.Series, out["close"].astype(float))

    weights = [0.5, 0.3, 0.2] if len(windows) == 3 else [1.0 / len(windows)] * len(windows)

    score = pd.Series(0.0, index=out.index, dtype=float)
    for window, weight in zip(windows, weights, strict=True):
        signed = _signed_efficiency_ratio(close, window)
        out[f"er_{window}"] = signed
        score = score + (signed * weight)

    shortest = min(windows)
    if "volume" in out.columns:
        volume = cast(pd.Series, out["volume"].astype(float))
        rolling_volume = volume.rolling(shortest, min_periods=1).mean()
        volume_factor = (volume / rolling_volume.clip(lower=1e-9)).fillna(1.0)
        volume_factor = volume_factor.clip(lower=0.5, upper=2.0)
    else:
        volume_factor = pd.Series(1.0, index=out.index, dtype=float)

    if "buyer_power_ratio" in out.columns:
        buyer_power = cast(pd.Series, out["buyer_power_ratio"].astype(float))
        buyer_power = buyer_power.fillna(1.0).clip(lower=0.5, upper=3.0) / 1.5
        buyer_power = buyer_power.clip(lower=0.5, upper=1.5)
    else:
        buyer_power = pd.Series(1.0, index=out.index, dtype=float)

    power = (score * 100.0 * volume_factor * buyer_power).clip(lower=-100.0, upper=100.0)
    out["movement_power_score"] = power
    return restore(frame, out)

def detect_swing_legs(frame: DataFrame, reversal_pct: float = 5.0) -> DataFrame:
    """Detect ZigZag swing legs from the ``close`` column.

    A percentage-reversal ZigZag is run over the closing prices.  A leg is
    confirmed whenever price reverses by at least ``reversal_pct`` from the
    running extreme; the final, still-active leg is appended so the output
    always ends at the last bar.  Input and output engine types match.

    Args:
        frame: A history frame containing ``close``.  ``date`` (used for
            ``start_date``/``end_date``) and ``volume`` (used for volume
            statistics) are optional; without ``date`` positional integer
            indexes are used, and without ``volume`` the volume columns are
            ``0.0``/``NaN``.
        reversal_pct: Minimum reversal, in percent, required to confirm a new
            pivot.  Must be positive.  Defaults to ``5.0``.

    Returns:
        One row per leg (completed legs plus the active leg) with columns:

        * ``leg_id`` (``int``) — one-based leg number.
        * ``direction`` (``int``) — ``1`` for up legs, ``-1`` for down legs.
        * ``start_date`` / ``end_date`` (``Any``) — values from ``date``, or
        positional indexes when ``date`` is absent.
        * ``start_price`` / ``end_price`` (``float``) — pivot prices.
        * ``leg_return_pct`` (``float``) — percentage price change over the leg.
        * ``leg_bars`` (``int``) — number of bars spanned (end index - start).
        * ``leg_velocity`` (``float``) — ``leg_return_pct / max(leg_bars, 1)``.
        * ``avg_volume`` (``float``) — mean volume across the leg's bars.
        * ``leg_volume_expansion`` (``float``) — this leg's ``avg_volume``
        divided by the previous leg's; ``NaN`` for the first leg or when the
        previous average is zero.

        An empty frame with the same columns is returned for empty input or
        when no pivots are found.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``reversal_pct <= 0``.
        KeyError: If the ``close`` column is missing.

    Examples:
        >>> legs = detect_swing_legs(iq.history("فولاد"), reversal_pct=5.0)
        >>> legs[["direction", "leg_return_pct", "leg_velocity"]].tail(5)
        >>> legs[legs["leg_volume_expansion"] > 1.5]["direction"].tolist()
    """

    if reversal_pct <= 0:
        raise ValueError("reversal_pct must be positive")

    source = to_pandas(frame)
    if source.empty:
        return empty_like(frame, LEG_COLUMNS)
    if "close" not in source.columns:
        raise KeyError("Missing required column: close")

    closes = source["close"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    dates: list[Any] = (
        source["date"].tolist() if "date" in source.columns else list(range(len(source)))
    )
    volumes = (
        source["volume"].astype(float).to_numpy()
        if "volume" in source.columns
        else np.zeros(len(source), dtype=float)
    )

    pivots = _zigzag(closes, reversal_pct / 100.0)
    legs: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for leg_id in range(1, len(pivots)):
        start_index, start_price = pivots[leg_id - 1]
        end_index, end_price = pivots[leg_id]
        if end_index <= start_index:
            continue
        direction = 1 if end_price >= start_price else -1
        return_pct = ((end_price / start_price) - 1.0) * 100.0 if start_price else 0.0
        bars = end_index - start_index
        avg_volume = float(np.mean(volumes[start_index : end_index + 1]))
        legs.append(
            {
                "leg_id": leg_id,
                "direction": direction,
                "start_date": dates[start_index],
                "end_date": dates[end_index],
                "start_price": start_price,
                "end_price": end_price,
                "leg_return_pct": return_pct,
                "leg_bars": bars,
                "leg_velocity": return_pct / max(bars, 1),
                "avg_volume": avg_volume,
                "leg_volume_expansion": float("nan"),
            }
        )

    for index in range(1, len(legs)):
        previous_volume = float(legs[index - 1]["avg_volume"])
        if previous_volume > 0:
            legs[index]["leg_volume_expansion"] = float(legs[index]["avg_volume"]) / previous_volume

    if not legs:
        return empty_like(frame, LEG_COLUMNS)
    result = pd.DataFrame(legs, columns=LEG_COLUMNS)
    return restore(frame, result)

def is_market_open(now: dt.datetime | None = None) -> bool:
    """Return True during Saturday-Wednesday TSETMC sessions (09:00-12:30 IRST).

    Python weekday numbering is Monday=0, so the active days are 5, 6, 0, 1
    and 2.  The time is interpreted in ``Asia/Tehran`` (with a fixed +03:30
    fallback when tzdata is unavailable).

    Args:
        now: Optional aware or naive datetime.  Naive values are assumed to be
            Tehran local time.  Defaults to the current instant.

    Returns:
        ``True`` when the current weekday is Saturday to Wednesday and the
        local time is between 09:00 and 12:30 inclusive, otherwise ``False``.

    Examples:
        >>> import datetime as dt
        >>> is_market_open(dt.datetime(2026, 10, 31, 10, 0))  # Saturday
        True
        >>> is_market_open(dt.datetime(2026, 10, 30, 13, 0))  # Friday
        False
    """

    timezone = _tehran_timezone()
    current = now or dt.datetime.now(timezone)
    if current.tzinfo is None:
        current = current.replace(tzinfo=timezone)
    current = current.astimezone(timezone)
    if current.weekday() not in {5, 6, 0, 1, 2}:
        return False
    current_time = current.time()
    return dt.time(9, 0) <= current_time <= dt.time(12, 30)

def _run_with_client(factory: Callable[[AsyncIranQuant], Awaitable[T]]) -> T:
